Is the optimization horrid? Yes, no game should rely on DLSS this much to the point where I have to resort to the performance preset for high with a 40 FPS cap, when most games on my setup run on ultra 60 fps owith DLSS set to balanced, if not higher. Is Randy Bitchford still an ass online? Also yes, BUT!

The game itself is miles ahead of 3 in every other aspect, the gameplay is fluid and way more balanced than 3, the world, or at least what I've seen of it so far, while less varied than 3 and definitely less varied than 2, the open world serves the game's structure well, especially for what the plot is doing.

This is going to be a little controversial, but i like the game's story, mostly because it shifts away from Pandora, away from msot of the familiar characters, and most improtantly, away from the shadow of Handsome Jack and the sirens. I like that it's a clean break from the past, and one sidequest in particular that doubles down on that aspect almost made me cry.

Or maybe I'm just glad I got it for like 25 bucks cause I would be pissed if I got it at full price lmao

I honestly like this BL4 as the next entry in the series. As someone who grew up watching my dad play BL2, I never got into that game thanks to having to play through the story three times to hit a true endgame. Mainly, I played BL3 and I loved that game. Was the main story the best in the series? No, but for me that didn't matter. Do I prefer linear maps compared to the open one here? Yes. I wish we got more linear maps with a theme/biome than what the DLC has given. Do I want to play more of BL4? Yes. Finding the time to play more of it is my main problem. I only really have four big negative feelings about this game. 

The Infamy system. 
Good Lord I hate it. Why can I not just play through the story at my own pace instead of having to take mandatory detours for side missions? Why did they make it punishing to play the main story when you are just trying to play quickly through a new character. C4sh for example. I played through the entire dlc he came with, which I loved, and just dropped the playthrough after it because coming back to the main game to play through each region sucks when I can't do it without facing enemies eight levels above me. This is my main reason why I haven't played so much of this game on Steam, I have more hours on the Xbox version. (Thank you for cross-character saves.)

Balancing Vault Hunters
This is just something I have never understood. I get fixing bugs and exploits related to their kit. A good dev team makes it clear what is a bug and what isn't. But why are we nerfing my boy Rafa's melee damage into the ground when he can still do quadrillion damage with a certain melee build. Punishing the whole of one tree just to stop a small subset of the player base from one-shotting bosses sucks. Vex is a can of buggy systems and glitches that I just don't want to get into. Especially the way Trouble has been handled. How can this elemental Tiger companion suck so much that the action skill is just useless at one point? I love the concept but I can't handle how bad Trouble is. Amon. He is still fun to play as in my opinion but feels just a bit weaker than the rest. I can say I had my most fun with Harlow and her entire three action skills. I hope the next dlc Vault Hunter is as good as C4sh is because that would pull me back in.

Pearls
Some are fun to play with. Some are nice nods to really strong guns in the franchise. HOWEVER, most are absolutely awful to play with. I feel like these very rare and grind filled guns should be stronger than most legendary weapons. (This is a problem in most of the Borderlands games if they have them.)

Enemy Variety
There is three Order, Ripper, and the Flora and Fauna of Kairos. They are very varied within the three factions but please add more than just the three of them. The Moxie DLC did add a new faction that I love to look and fight but they are stuck to the DLC.

I love Borderlands 4 and hope that it will be a better game in the end. Buy it if it is on sale if you've never played a Borderlands game before but if you liked the combat of BL3 over BL2 play this one and have fun.

Borderlands 3 does everything better than this game. If you didn't tell me, I'd say this was the prequel to that game. Not nostalgia. I played them back to back. Borderlands 3 looks better, better story, better loot, better guns, better enemies. 

A lot of this game seems to be locked behind a paywall too. I bought a gun with 2/3rds of my in-game money and then it said it would just sit locked in my inventory until I buy some DLC with real money. I had already beat the story so that was my quitting point.
if you're an insomniac, i would recommend this game. it put me to sleep every time i tried to play it.

I'll start with my 3 biggest gripes so far in the game, and then talk about what I like

1- The complete removal of shared loot.  All drops are instanced now, and it makes it an absolute pain if you are playing for fun to share things with friends, as a gun that might be an upgrade for them is just junk to you and you barely look at it when you auto sell it.  I understand why the people grinding bosses for rare drops prefer this, but what was wrong with having it as an option like in BL3?

2- The car system. Another one where I get the intention behind having everyone have their own summonable mount, but once again when you play with friends it makes travel to new locations (through very boring routes I add) extra tedious and disjointed.  I miss being able to share cars with friends as they man the gun or ride in the back while we drive around as a group, just kills the vibe of us actually working together and makes it feel like its 4 people that happen to be at the same spot rather than working together.

3- The way the open world makes the story feel.  The open world isn't a bad idea in concept, but what it managed to do in this game was kill any association I had with certain areas with certain characters, which made the characters more forgettable.  When the whole map blends together as you go around, the characters become a blur too.  I could go on a rant about character writing as well, but that's always been hit or miss since even BL1 days.  Good and bad characters are everywhere, but they made even the good characters forgettable by removing easy ways to associate areas with them.

What I like
In an effort to be fair there are some things I like about the game, the combat (when you find a gun that doesn't feel garbage to use) is actually pretty fun, the character animations for getting hit by crits and stuff make you feel like you are actually impacting them. there are also still some good sidequests out there, like helping a missile explode, that reminds you there is still some comedy out there in this game if you search for it.
I also enjoy that the big boss fights are generally more than just "burst the guy down instantly", and that they added phases to the fight for the major bosses.  Makes them way more interesting to do.
The last thing I can say is they made it so you can make claptrap have no audio, my ears are saved.

As for performance, I'm on a pretty overkill PC (9800x3D and 9070XT) and I haven't had tons  of issues now, this long after release.  It's still not the best running game ever, but at least it's not crashing, just constantly compiling shaders lol.

All in all, if you have friends willing to slog through this with you, and you get it on a DEEP sale, it can be worth it.  But I just don't see the appeal of the normal end game slog or going through the motions of UVHM when this is the story you play through.
Story is alright. Best gunplay from any borderlands, but would be better if after changing settings I didnt need to load my shaders everytime

Borderlands 4 is definitely a mixed bag. However, as a casual fan of the series, I can recommend this game to casual fans of Borderlands and looter shooters. I only have the base game, so this review is only for the content in the current base game. 

TLDR: If you are a fan of looter shooters and have typically enjoyed the previous Borderlands games, you will have fun with this one. You can take your time with the content (by the way you don't have to do EVERY single activity in a region before moving on to the next) and there are lots of builds/loot to experiment with. The story is significantly darker and more reminiscent of the earlier games in the franchise, which is a plus from the over the top characters from Borderlands 3. Overall, one playthrough of this game will easily get you tons of hours of looting. 

PROS: 
1. The Gameplay: Each new Borderlands game has improved upon the gameplay mechanics of the previous game, and this game is easily the best in the series in terms of this. The grapple hook and jet pack (that has a quick dash) add a lot more verticality/speed to the combat. The guns feel great to use and each manufacturer has a distinct feel when using them (Jacobs vs Order for example). 
2. The Encore Machine: This is easily the greatest addition to the Borderlands series. One of my main complaints of the previous games has been that saving and quitting is very time consuming for farming for certain gear/loot. With this encore machine, you pay a small fee and can immediately start a new attempt at a boss. Farming bosses for loot has never been easier and you can see all of the various loot you have received from all of the farming you have done. Genuinely a great improvement for the series as a whole.
3. The Ordinance: This is a subjective one, but I was a never a fan of using Rocket Launchers in the previous Borderlands games (especially in early game) as they had very little ammo and each Rocket ammo would cost a substantial amount. However, now that they have grenades/throwables/rocket launchers as a cooldown, I have used them substantially more than the previous games combined. I really enjoy the variety in them as well (throwing knives, laser rockets, different types of grenades). 
4. The Vault Hunters: This is yet another subjective one, but I have enjoyed using all of the Vault Hunters in this game (with the exception of the two DLC characters as I don't have them). They each have a variety of skills that are fun to use. Also, the voice actors did a phenomenal job with showcasing their personalities.
5. The Bosses: There are bosses for the story, the Vaults, the Raids, the Auger mines, and more that require you to use the new movement system. The bosses even appear in the open world as Rifts, which means there is always loot to be farmed! 
6). The Side-Characters: Very subjective, but I had a great time meeting/learning about the side characters of Kairos. Even some of the characters from the side missions were memorable (highlighting the psycho with his robotic legs questline). However, there were some characters like Zadra and [spoiler]Arjay[/spoiler] that ultimately fall flat and definitely required more time with them. 
7). Toned-Down Story: After Borderlands 3's very over-the-top villains, Borderlands 4 has villains that are more closer to the earlier titles. I am especially referring to the characters of Vile Lictor and Callis, who have interesting storylines where you learn about their origins and how they were impacted by the cataclysm.

MIXED/NEUTRAL: 

1. The Main Story: Borderlands 4 story, in my opinion, is better than the base story of Borderlands 3. However, there are some issues. 
     
 a). The Timekeeper: The Timekeeper is a great villain at the start who is vastly different than the Twins from B3 and Handsome Jack from B2. However, after the intro, he takes a back seat when you are going through the different zones in the story. He will occasionally appear to make remarks, but you don't feel his presence while going through like 85% of the story. It definitely feels like he could have been utilized a lot more, especially if as he says is "always watching". Also, the fact that he doesn't he even try to do anything about this growing Resistance until the very end is very odd (like he could have taken out all of the factions in like a second,  [spoiler]which he demonstrates at the end[/spoiler]). After you learn more about him, it becomes even more apparent that he should have made more appearances throughout the story so that the end could have had a better impact. 
    
 b). Kairos Uprising/Kairos Resistance: After you save all of the three regions from their respective villain, we definitely should have had more time with the characters from each region talking/interacting with one another. Even though we "unite" all of Kairos, it definitely does not feel like it as we don't see any interactions between them. They are not even present during the final missions of the story, which is a huge letdown (they are just on ECHO). 
    
c). Non-Linear Story: Since you can tackle any region in any order, your actions have no consequence on any other region. You will occasionally hear NPCs mention that you took out another region leader, but that's about it. 

2. The Open World: On your first playthrough, discovering Kairos is great as there are lots of points of interest (Vault pieces, Auger mines, Drill sites, etc.). However, there are very little dynamic activities (Rifts & OpenWorld Events - one for each region). There are no enemies on vehicles (besides Order machines/tanks) or no incentives to get involved in the fights that occur throughout the world. Overall, the open world could have more dynamic elements (such as the bounties being offered while you just drive around the world).

CONS/NEGATIVES:
1. Vehicles: Besides appearance, all of the vehicles don't have much differences from one another. The weapons don't do much damage (especially on higher levels) and they don't offer much besides traversal. This was a letdown as it could have been used for so much more (racing events or more vehicular combat with each vehicle having their own special ability). 
2. Enemy Variety: You will mainly encounter 3 enemies: Rippers, wildlife, and the Order. The majority of the time it feels like you are battling the Order, which can become stale pretty fast. It seems like they are fixing this with the DLCs, but for the base game, it is mainly the Order enemies.  
3. Optimization/Performance: Even though I have not encountered any issues, this game does require a lot of shader compiling in the beginning. Additionally, this game requires some sort of DLSS or FSR upscaling to run at decent frame rates. The performance is substantially better than at launch, but I know that lots of people have/are still encountering issues. 
4.  No Homebase: This is subjective, but there is no homebase that you go back to after important missions, which was Sanctuary for both Borderlands 2 and 3. As a result, you don't have a common area where you might see NPCs have important conversations (this goes back to the lack of a "United Kairos") or where story events take place. 

CONCLUSION: 

Borderlands 4 is a solid entry to the series. Gearbox tried something new with the open world - some of it worked and some of it didn't. The side missions, characters, loot, and gameplay are definitely the highlights. Great job on the game and excited to see the next one! Thank you for reading my review if you got to the end!

Overall the game is fine but I'm not rushing to play it. It's by far the worst out of all of them imo.  The open world aspect was a miss because you don't get that unique encounter vibe when you would travel to different locations from the previous installments. The encounters you get throughout the map get old quick and the itch to keep coming back to play gradually dwindles over time. i can kind of see the vision of trying something new with the open world concept but it misses what made borderlands borderlands and the typical loot mechanic isnt enough to save it. With that the u.i. menus are absolutely abysmal. They are lazy and not uniquely attractive like previous titles. I lack interest in trying out different skill trees because I'm just trying to get out of the menus as fast as possible. It's not very interactive world wise as the previous titles either like having a main base to work from and interacting with the unique npcs. The world is just empty with enemies thrown in between to have something to shoot at. And exploration is a joke. There are so many invisible barriers blocking you from taking "short cuts" so you're forced to travel all the way around to get to certain things when you could have just climbed over some rock formation to get to the other side. The barriers make sense for the outer edge of the map to keep us in sure but everything on the inside where you think you can just travel over quickly is met with a hard "denied go the long way." I though it was supposed to be "open" world?

Overall they should have just kept to the core of borderlands with it's normal unique playstyle and teleports to different maps instead of the open world concept. I want to like it and enjoy it but every time I log on I'm just as quickly logging off because it's just not hitting that itch yeah know? Finished Borderland 4, And it was pretty disappointing despite buying the deluxe edition for half off, Let’s Start with the Story and Characters which are step up and step down, While Borderlands 3 was pretty cringe with the GenZ and Millennial writing that plagued the Dialogue, there was more of an attempt to make the Villains have some form of personality and background The Story doesn’t really try to bridge the events from after Borderlands 3 or explain why we moved from Pandora or give any type of Background info on the Order and how it established itself on this new setting and why Kairos is the central setting compared to the previous games that would do this, None of the characters here or even the TimeKeeper don’t stick in your mind and not that memorable, Arjay was just a nothing character despite the writers really wanting to be that corrupted character that shows up, Lilith is just there and Amara is there to be the sirens to do things, The Ripper Queen was kinda an interesting character

This was Lowkey even more disappointing than 3, The Story barely even explains the gap between this and 3, The Open World is a Massive step down due to being reduced to only 4 zones and the scale tries to be back to basics but it just slows a huge lack of variety compared to traveling to different Planets in 3 and it was genuinely more varied in locations and settings and up the actual scale and in 2 the DLC took to really different places and Zones that gave Pandora depth, Kairos just barely has any depth to the setting and gets dull traversing where the only difference is grass, dessert, and snow and there’s no difference to these settings and the only variety is found inside the Order City and Fortress

The Enemy variety is actually terrible since for 100 hours you going to be killing the same Order Enemies and Rippers Again and Again and Again and the same Grunts and 3 Variations and it gets so boringly monotonous and the occasional wild life like the previous games did not have this issue due to each zone Having Enemies that would be more reflective of the zone, You don't even get to fight any Eridians that would occupy the vaults in this game not even in the Primordial Vaults it's still the same enemies you fought out side 

The Gameplay easily gets Broken because you're able to get access to Legendary weapons with way more ease compared to earlier games and it just breaks the gameplay loop,you don't have to constantly manage your resources, be on the hunt for rare loot since you have the best weapons already and you can breeze through the game on HARD mode, Constantly looking for Ammo and Money etc, This makes the In game economy just feels borderline pointless due to this too since you don't have to horde loot to sell off to get better loot and consumables like in Previous games and experiment with weapons, You’re basically a super hero rather than a Merc earning money and loot and it’s feels handed to u 

Side Quests start off VERY repetitive in the Grass area of Kairos due to keep finding the drones and taking them to areas and the other one reattaching a ripper with his Legs and barely do any interesting stuff compared to the other 2 areas  

It does the Annoying thing in Tiny Tina Wonderlands where the level scaling is just constantly tailored to your level which just erases all forms of difficulty where you're constantly fighting enemies at your rank like there aren't dedicated areas with specifically low level enemies and vice versa with high level like the previous games, you can't really have any power progression this way, I want to feel more powerful as a player 

The Optimization is Pretty bad at points when it comes to compiling shaders and the game shutting down and restarting, having to turn up the volume on my PC to get the sound working, and the FPS ranging from 30 fps to 80 FPS at points 

6/10

The game is poorly optimized and this, i think, is not something new. It's unplayable without framegen and even then, you can still end up with a rather poor experience due to the nature of the tech itself. 

Story wise, BL4 is, probably, the worst out of all of them. Moving from a linear storytelling to an open world one was a very bad decision. It gave me Destiny 2 PTSD with their "Go and grab this then come back". 

The gunplay itself is decent. Not great, not terrible but far from what other games have implemented (like the previously mentioned Destiny 2 and more recently, Witchfire). So if you're after some good gunplay, go check those two out. 

The graphics themselves are, again, decent. This time, it seems, they really chose to stick with the Red color way too much. On an oled panel, this might begin to be bothersome. 

Another issue that i have been having are the constant crashes. Regardless of the settings i have chose to play at, the game will crash. It's just a matter of time. I tried undervolting/underclocking/power limiting both my CPU and GPU and still wasn't able to avoid the crashes. Worst part of it all is that with the most recent one, i have also lost my savegame file. Gone are close to 30 hours invested into this so called game.

Picked this up on sale after a long wait. The mixed reviews made me curious, and I just missed playing some Borderlands. For context: 500+ hours in BL3 on Epic and 200+ in BL2, so I know what this franchise is and what it isn't.

The crashes sting even more because of how odd the respawn points are: they're scattered across the map as bus stops, and if you don't hit one on your way to some far corner and then die or crash, you're redoing the whole journey. Respawns take longer too. To be fair, the more you play the less you die, as you gear up and get good. And the endgame is fun. and if you ve played basically everything mentioned and you still crave BL content, try giving modding a chance(BL2 has a ton of replayability making it worth completing many more playthroughs after getting bored of the base game)

But if you still intend on paying for BL4 i recommand waiting for a hefty discount to get your money's worth.

I struggled to get into Borderlands 4 at first. I put somewhere around 10–20 hours into it, found myself getting bored, and eventually set it down for about 10 months. I recently decided to give it another shot, and this time it finally clicked. More importantly, I figured out why I struggled with it so much the first time.

I’ve been playing Borderlands since day one and have played through every game in the series. Over the years, I developed a pretty specific way of playing them: enter an area, pick up every quest, challenge, and task available, complete everything, and then move on. That approach absolutely killed Borderlands 4 for me. This is the first truly open-world Borderlands, so there aren’t the same clearly segregated zones with a manageable list of things to knock out before moving on. There is a ton of stuff scattered around the world, and trying to complete everything as I encountered it turned the game into a repetitive grind. I was spending hours doing side activities while barely advancing the story, and eventually I just stopped caring.

When I came back to it, I changed my approach. I started following the main story and only doing the occasional side quest, challenge, or activity as I came across them. Suddenly, I was having fun. I’m enjoying the story, the combat feels great, and I actually want to keep playing. All of those other quests, challenges, and activities aren’t going anywhere, and I can go back and knock them out during the endgame instead of burning myself out trying to clear the map as I go.

If you’re a longtime Borderlands player who normally approaches these games the same way I do and you’re struggling to get into Borderlands 4, stop trying to clear everything before moving on. Follow the story and let the rest happen naturally. It completely changed the game for me.

This game is better than Borderlands 3 in every single way. The gunplay, the story, ... everything. It's not that high of a bar, but still.

Where it falls apart is in performance and stability. I would pick 4 over 3 every single day, but I have to admit 4 is barely playable. The outlines of everything flicker constantly, assets take way too long to load in even on an SSD and LoD stays on the lowest setting for AGES when you get close and I'm not sure whether I should still cause the stuttering "stuttering", because some time it takes so long to resolve it's more like "freezing". Exceeding 60fps without DLSS is basically impossible without dropping to 1080p.

Steam SAYS it's Deck Verified, but that's a lie. Not only is performance horrendous (25fps max, not clean), but Gearbox in its infinite wisdom thought it would be a good idea to REMOVE ALL GRAPHICS SETTINGS from the menu for Deck users. I assume they thought Deck users craved the limitations of console gaming (a baffling assumption), but instead of simplifying the experience, they guaranteed the only way for Deck users to get a remotely playable experience was by going into desktop mode and messing with the game files to mod it into a playable state, or trick the game into thinking it's not running on a Steam Deck through launch options to reveal the options menu again. That is the opposite of simplifying anything.

It is such a bad decision I'm wondering under my tinfoil hat whether Randy made it intentionally terrible just to sabotage the game on Deck just because he hates Valve. It's so bad on paper, so terrible in practice and so universally unpopular in the community, it's hard not to assume malice at this point.

...but again, the game is actually good under that. Some bossfights are the best the series has ever seen. It's such a shame it's in such a terrible technical state to this day, because I probably would recommend it otherwise.

This game has the same issues as Destiny. Stellar gameplay on top of an abysmal story and hostile cash-grab DLC.

[b]The Good[/b]

Is moving around and shooting in this game absolute top-tier? Oh yes. I've spent far more time with this game than I should have for this single fact alone. Unfortunately, that is where this good review ends.

[b]The Bad[/b]

The story is abominable and easily the worst in the entire Borderlands franchise. I've played through the main game start to finish and I still don't know or care who the Timekeeper was except for being the detached voice that would dump exposition at the exact wrong moments in the game. I'm fighting two dozen baddies with screen-painting explosions and ear rending sound effects and suddenly I hit a hidden trigger point and all I can hear in the background is bog-standard sinister mumbling about something I can't understand over the combat sounds and honestly don't care about. Let me be clear, this isn't Handsome Jack taunting us in a glib and funny way while we traverse the icy wastes of Pandora. This is some unknown copy/paste big baddie who is dumping tons of plot-crucial exposition while I'm trying to engage with the game's one actual strength. One certainly gets the impression that the writers of BL4 never heard the axiom "Show, don't tell."

In truth, it feels like BL4 is intended as a reset that never actually pulled the trigger. We cold open on a completely new world that has never once been directly mentioned and everyone except the literal most annoying character in the franchise is completely MIA. The player spends easily half the game before we see any familiar faces from previous franchise entries, and we are forced to catch up on lore that has nearly zero connective tissue to previous games. We're not shown any of the developments that lead the OG cast to Kairos, and explanations are hand-waved so quickly it's beyond an afterthought. Secondary and tertiary characters are just...missing, with no leads, story arcs, or reasoning, and as we can later see, it's because many of them have been reserved for paid DLC. 

Even new characters such as Arjay are treated as throwaway fodder, who guides us through the tutorial, spends a small amount of story time with the player, and then vanishes through a plot device before popping up again later. Also, while we're on the subject of plot devices, (spoiler) [spoiler]control bolts are the clumsiest implementation of "would you kindly?" I've ever seen, and don't even succeed as a plot device because we defy the Timekeeper for 99% of the game, even during lynchpin moments where the vault hunters would be handily defeated with a single well-timed control command[/spoiler]. To say this aspect of the plot is disappointing is like saying the Borderlands movie was kinda bad; an understatement so heavy it could collapse spacetime. To round out my criticism of the writing, characters are painfully one-dimensional, especially returning cast who we have come to know very well via previous games. [spoiler]Lilith[/spoiler] in particular has seemed to just get worse and worse with each game, becoming more polarized and flat every time we see her rear her ugly head. With each iteration she just gets less fun to have around and by BL4, her cardboard cutout is an actual drag on the story. Also, aesthetic changes are just atrocious, with characters exhibiting "growth" simply by having longer hair or new beards. Updated character designs are uninspired and fall into a category labelled "changes that were made simply because someone got paid (poorly) to make them." Basically, everyone is unlikable, and nothing is done over the course of the game to change that.

The art direction is...fine. It's the comic book inspired textures that Borderlands has become known for, only now with shinies, sparklies, and neon particles. No piece of architecture truly inspires awe, and no weapon, baddie, or vehicle is interesting enough to comment. It seems like the entire game was funded from a grant/bribe by Big Triangle, as pretty much everywhere you look there's butt-loads of the three-sided shapes making up everything from wall accents to UI effects to loading screens. I've spent a little over 100 hours in the game as of this writing, and let me tell you, triangles get old.

Voice acting is similarly okay; nothing is truly inspired or heartfelt, and even the best on offer such as Claptrap and Moxxie sound like they're counting down until the weekend hits. As mentioned above, the Timekeeper doesn't even rank, his voice is so disappointingly predictable and "baddiefied" that I can't listen to more than a couple lines before rolling my eyes. He sounds like every Disney villain ever, except that he can't enunciate or project his voice or leverage any tone aside from "cartoonish scowl." 

All in all, I simply cannot recommend this game to anyone with even a passing love of Borderlands, as the heart has been sucked completely out of this iteration of the universe, leaving a game that probably would have been a banger with literally any other IP attached to it. As it stands though, if this is the direction Borderlands is heading, they just lost a longtime fan.

[b]The Ugly[/b]

As an aside: I feel like more than just this game hurt this game, and I do believe much of the blame lies with Gearbox head Randy Pitchford, as he has inserted himself relentlessly into the discourse ever since the movie (rightly) flopped. He has been weirdly antagonistic of the player base, like a DM who knows he's going to wipe the entire party in a D&D game, and can't hold in his excitement at that fact. From telling us how much we should like the flaming trainwreck of a movie (and how we're wrong if we don't), to being quoted as saying "Real gamers will find a way to pay" for the game at any price, Pitchford has singlehandedly done more to erode the Borderlands brand than any combination of in-game gaffes. I can't be the only longtime fan who has been turned off of Gearbox's efforts by Pitchford's incessant social media tantrums. Also, *Randy* my computer specs are perfectly fine, and that was proven out by the fact that a year down the line from release, the game has received multiple optimization patches in direct contravention of Randall Steward Pitchford II's assertions that I needed stronger hardware because the game was just too much for my rig. Go eat a stinkbug Randy, you lying, disingenuous bowl of scummy lukewarm dogwater.

All I need now is for someone to mod the QoL changes and gameplay of BL4 into the story and world of BL2 and we'll have something approaching the perfect game. I know that'll never happen, but it's more fun to dream about that than to slog through BL4's story again.

[h2] Story [/h2]

Firstly, [b] the story is not as bad as Borderlands 3. [/b] 

That said, it sufferes from incoherency due to the open world nature of the game. The game starts out in one zone, splits into three that you can choose to complete in your own order, and then returns to one for the finale. The issue is that this means things feel 'stale' once you branch out into the 'choose which zone to go' section. Each story has to be self-contained becauase you can complete them in any order resulting in it feeling like taking a step back each time you move onto the next one to clear it which is very jarring. 

It also leads to some characters or parts feeling easy to forget as whichever zone you complete first will be the furthest on your mind as you get to the finale. There were real opportunities to weave in story telling with the open world setting but Borderlands 4 falls short of this.

 [h2] Gameplay [/h2]

The gameplay is a nice improvement. Medkits becoming an individual cooldown and grenades no longer being limited by ammo but instead on a timer means you get to use them both a lot more often. The new 'Ordinance' system is a lot of fun and is a great change. Weapons also have attatchments again like in 3, they're very powerful and have their own cooldown of sorts. The skill trees are interesting and there's a lot of variation for you to indulge in. 

The issue for me was, if you do utilize everything to its fullest you end up becoming very powerful, [b]too powerful.[/b] I played Vex the Siren and I made my build on my own, leveling up things and choosing synergistic options to the point where I played 80% of the game without a gun in order to weaken myself, and still it was too easy. It was a Melee reaper build. As cool as it was waltzing through a setpiece whilst my reapers reaped the build I sowed, it trivialized the content. 

I wish there were greater difficulty options to add more of a challenge. If you're half-decent at build crafting and read everything in your tree before you level, you might run into this issue.

 [h2] Misc Positives & Negatives [/h2]

+The settings menu was nicely made and fun to fiddle around with to figure out what I liked. 
+The game is graphically pretty.
+Sound is great/fine.
+Movement system had fun upgrades
+The bigger boss battles had cool mechanics (even if they died too fast for me to need to use them)

-You can't ride in cars with another player like you can in the older games.
-The open world dilutes the experience instead of broadening it.
-Getting drops for a DLC character you don't own is awful.
-The price is just way too high in conjunction with expensive DLC's


 [h2] Conclusion [/h2]

The story is better than 3's but it suffers from the game being open world and falls short of delivering on what it offers. There's lot of questionable things where if you think about it for too long you'll just be frustrated by the convenience the plot demands. 

The gameplay is great but again, due to the open world, I'd almost find replaying through Borderlands 3 DLC's more enjoyable. The level like structure was traded in for something just not as fleshed out unfortunately and the replayability suffers for it.

Ultimately, if it wasn't asking you to pay such a premium price (in both game and DLC) for a middling Borderlands experience, I might've recommended it.

A big step up from BL3. The game still suffers from underutilized characters and storytelling issues, but Borderlands 4 is richer in narrative. Consistently solid and brilliant in places. Finale suffers in its execution but the Timekeeper is the best character this franchise has had since Handsome Jack.

Everything about him is so succinct but loaded, the total opposite of how modern Borderlands characters are. The vault hunters are in cutscenes sure, but the Timekeeper is BL4's main character. Despite not getting much actual screentime, every villain, location, all put a magnifying lens on how he ticks. You see the effects of the hurt he's done to the planet's citizens and those close to him. But also glimpses on how much he's hurting himself, how much he's convinced himself playing fair justifies his own suffering. Makes for a decently compelling narrative about powerlessness and how we cope with it.

While the story is solid, the game is held back by not being great in other areas. Discovery gets undercut by collectibles. Exploring doesn't feel organic or exciting. Vault hunter abilities become less fun the more you progress. Pearls and phosphenes are poorly executed, and the lack of storytelling through loot only compounds it. Reducing the drop rates just isn't enough to make items feel special, the sauce of BL1/BL2's treasure hunt isn't there. Sadly there are many things that sour the experience, but when Borderlands 4 is good, it's good!

After playing for 178 hours I think I can write some thoughts about the game. Generally it's very fun to play and gameplay-wise I like it. Movement is great, guns are good and it's nice to see some QoL features added like Big Encore Machines and saving collectibles from other save files. But there are a few moments that I think were poorly implemented

I have a laptop below minimum requirements and it runs the game on the very minimum FHD settings, which is surprisingly nice. I've played it on a high end PC and it doesn't look that good even on badass settings at 4K resolution. I would say it's like a Borderlands 3 with better lighting. All the UE5 nanites and stuff isn't required for this game. People like the Borderlands games for gameplay and/or story. 

And yeah... story. We all remember that abomination of BL3 main story line and I would say they did better in this one, but still it's not good. Most of the story is lackluster. It's like: to kill the big guy you need to kill 3 other, then rekill one of them and here you are at the top of the tower. The ending is a bit weird because you just get some useless thing and then one character says "I think we got what we came for". The End. At least they didn't make the villain that obnoxious, but he appears for a few dialogues and then he's like: "Oh, you're here... let's fight". He can control people with bolts, but it seems like he's not in the mood for it)

Also the world. I don't like the idea of the open world. It feels empty and useless. All locations look almost the same. The fauna consists of literally 4 animals: kratches (like rakks), manglers (like skaggs, but they are cats), creeps (like ratches or varkids) and wildhorns, which are the only one not copy-pasted from previous games. Mobs also include rippers (like bandits) and the order (like hyperion in bl2 with a few new enemies). You will see order and ripper mobs throughout the whole game, including all bounty packs. Most of the bosses are actually chunkier versions of normal mobs and are very boring. Vehicles are generic, but not bad. They just look different, but feel absolutely the same. I think implementing vehicles from BL3 with summoning them from any place would be a better idea.

The last thing I want to complain about is legendaries and pearls. I love that we finally get pearls after all these years, but the first pearl I got was a world drop at level 11... And it's not my luck it's just how it is in this game. I've got like 50 world drop pearls in one playthrough. Legendaries are also common here. Not like in BL3, but still common. I would like to decrease the world drop chance of legendaries and pearls to make it feel more special. Also dedicated drop chances are broken. As far as I know the chance of dropping a dedicated legendary is 23% on UVH 7 and the chance for a dedicated pearl is 0.95%. Maybe I'm bad at math, but getting a pearl every 5-8 kills is not 0.95% (it's from Origo). Also some dedicated legendaries drop more often than others. I farmed Origo a lot and I noticed that Watts 4 Dinner drops are less common than Bottled Lightning or Kaoson. Class mod drops are also weird, because the chance of dropping a class mod not for your character on UVH 7 is 1,435% * 4 = 5,74% and for your character is 17,25%, but you get almost the same amount of both!!! One time I got three legendaries from a boss and all of them were world drops!

That's it! The problems that I described are not huge problems. I still think this is a great game and I want people to remember it as such. It is possible for Borderlands 4 to be even a greater game in the future, but looking at the current set of DLC's it is hard to see that future

I wanted to like this game. I REALLY did. I like the Gunplay and the Vault Hunters are fun. The guns are the best they have ever been and the movement system is way better than even 3s. I also have enjoyed every other Borderlands with three being my favorite (minus the story - the ONLY downside to three)...
HOWEVER:
This game is designed from the bottom up to waste your time. You cant skip dialogue even in second playthroughs, there are MANY times the game just has you standing there listening to terrible skits as you wait for your next quest marker, to activate the thing you need to for a mission but cant until characters stop their yapping... long death animations and respawns, few fast travel points on a map that requires you to tediously drive across the map.

Farming - what BL games are designed for (allegedly) also has these time wasting issues with bosses that have complete damage immunity for large sections of the fight, long dying animations instead of just dropping the (very terrible) loot. Play on UVHM6 - the highest difficulty - and you are rewarded with three blue items, two purple items and some ammo. Legendary Gear - even terrible ones - drop so rarely that you could spend 6 hours farming and only get a few and since multiple legendary items can drop from the SAME boss, you have like a 1/5 chance the legendary being dropped is the TYPE of item you want... and it has trash stats so its useless. MANY Legendary items CATEGORIES (such as Enhancements and CLASS MODS) have NO dedicated drop source so getting those is damn near impossible to target farm for... Build crafting is varied and numerous but CONSISTANTLY held back by poor drop rates and terrible dedicated drop allocations. Fast travel to the boss (or even the dungeon in which the boss resides) is not a thing in BL4. Instead you fast travel to the NEAREST unlockable base and have to DRIVE and run to the dungeon THEN run through the dungeon just to get to the boss room. This can take upwhere of thre to five minutes. Dont leave farming boss A to farm boss B; Youll have to run to BOTH bosses every time you switch from the "nearest" base... NO fast travel points anywhere NEAR any of the bosses. Another Time Waster. 

The open world is Meh. They need to return to the old map style. MANY of the games issues stem from this decision. Performance would be better if we had LOAD SCREENS between the (only) three regions. (I dont count the center region as its considerably smaller than the other REAL regions... and has only like two main story quests.) The world is empty of distinguishing and notable locations and you have Main Characteritis.... You get the ONLY vehicle on the planet - in this open world game. No roaming enemies in vehicles. 

Performance: Expect to use Frame Gen if you want higher than 70fps. I have a BEAST of a machine and still needed frame gen to reach higher than 100fps. Utter Craptastic performance. Even now. 

TLDR: game wastes LOTS of Time - Some would even say its a Premium Time-waster - and while it has really great gunplay and the vault hunters ARE fun to level... once you get into the weeds of Min Max and specialized farming... the game falls apart rapidly. Farming just is NOT rewarding in any way in BL4... I have played for 414 hours and feel like farming is a waste of time. after 414 hours i could not get ONE character to have the gear i set out to get. Wonderlands felt better to farm for legendary gear than in BL4... Premium Disappointment. Remove Randy from the studio... PLEASE!

Fun, fast-paced, pretty, and perhaps too big - Borderlands 4 is more Borderlands in every way.

Pro: It looks beautiful. With my RTX3070 I was only able to run it on medium, but the art style is very forgiving and even on medium it looked great. Ran pretty smoothly too, despite the complaints about performance that scared me off of purchasing it sooner.

Pro: Your Vault Hunter actually feels like they're in the world. The fact that they appear in cutscenes cannot be overstated with regards to how much that improved my sense of immersion and participation in the events of the game. Previous games (looking at you especially, BL3) had cutscenes just play out where it was like your character just became a pair of eyeballs with no agency whatsoever until you regained control of them, and that was so off-putting. But here your VH is actually taking part in the story. 10/10, please continue this in future games.

Pro: The tone is much more serious and much less a barrage of slapstick cringe toilet humour. The Timekeeper is a decent villain, and his generals are interesting and well designed. I liked that some of the missions were allowed to just be emotional - as they should be in this broken, cataclysmic world - without needing to be funny at all. There's still plenty of humour, but it's not drowning every moment of the experience.

Pro: Related to the above point, the characters. There was some great voice acting. I really enjoyed the new folks like Rush, Levaine, Defiant Calder, Callis, Vile Lictor, the Boss, Daphne, and others, and of course it was wonderful to have Zane back and to have him and Amara bouncing off each other.

Pro: Loot. So much loot. There are more combinations of stuff than ever, with different parts from different manufacturers being found on the same item, and the addition of firmware for your customization pleasure. Some great weapon designs and reload animations. Your mileage may definitely vary on this, but I liked the change with ordnance being on a cooldown, as it actually made me more likely to use my grenades when they were up.

Pro: The moment to moment gameplay is awesome. The increased mobility of the glide pack is super fun in combat, the butt slam returns (though the recovery animation is a bit too slow IMO), and it feels more fun than ever to leap into a gunfight, spray enemies with bullets, slide, duck behind cover, grapple a gas tank and hurl it at an enemy, and be dazzled by all those brightly coloured numbers filling your screen. I love the grapple and the verticality it brought to environments, and I enjoyed how the platforming was woven into everything. Sue me, I like climbing.

Con: The open world. I like the idea of an open world, but in reality there's long empty stretches and way too many invisible walls placed so that you can't just glide or climb somewhere you think you should be able to get to, which forces you to take the long way around. Even with your instantly summonable vehicle and its increased boost it still takes too long to get places. Kairos isn't Tamriel, where you're reading books and digging through everyone's furniture - you're primarily just trying to get somewhere to kill something. Maybe there was a happy medium to be found between hubs/zones and this fully open world, but I'm not sure it was hit here.

Con: Claptrap. Here's a hot take: I love Claptrap. Or I did, anyway - the Claptrap of 1 and 2 and even the Pre-Sequel, before his character seemed to become solidified into "the annoying useless guy everyone hates". I miss when he was just a friendly little robot trying to be helpful and open doors (and actually being great at his job, I might add). Now it seems like the devs are trying to purposely maximize his annoyance to the point where he has a whole separate volume slider just for him. Stop making me hate Claptrap, it feels bad.

Con: The epilogue ending. We have been receiving dire warnings of war coming since the end of the first Borderlands. We are five mainline games in - can the war please just come already? How many more games is this same can going to be kicked down the road?

Bugs: So, the ending bugged out for me, which was a major letdown. I killed the Timekeeper, entered the Vault, and...nothing. The scene that is supposed to play out in there never did, the chests were locked, and I just ended up travelling back to the world with no loot, no answers, and [spoiler]no final encounter with Arjay[/spoiler]. I have no idea why that happened, and nothing worked to fix it. Other than that, Vile Lictor didn't spawn in his boss fight, but a quit/reload fixed that just fine.

Ultimately, as someone who loves Borderlands, I had a pretty great time with BL4, and I'm looking forward to the upcoming level cap increase and the new VH.

All in all, better than 3, worse than 2.

Borderlands 4 is unsurprisingly the most divisive entry in the series since... well, the last numbered one but for very different reasons. gone is the obnoxious comedic writing of 3's horrible story, yet gone also is damn near any scrap of Borderlands' signature idiosyncrasies. 4 is comparatively - comparatively i stress - humourless, for the most part playing its new "we didn't play Far Cry guys honest" open-world story premise straighter than even the original game. while i certainly would've begged for this change during the lows of 3's misery, this over-corrects into being just plain boring, an issue Borderlands seemed incapable of having.

it feels pointless to describe the series' FPS/RPG trappings by now, since anybody reading reviews here is probably familiar with them. safe to say, BL4's rendition is an improvement on 3's already excellent formula. the guns have seen smart changes like manufacturer parts adding secondary fires unique to each while also receiving an extra layer of polish. they all feel wonderful to fire, as does ragdolling the game's bestiary. i also found my vault hunter's (Rafa) skilltrees to be loads of fun to mess around with, eventually settling on a laser-beam-status-inflicting-infinite-ammo mix that amazingly kept me engaged from start to finish alone.

i say amazingly because BL4's aforementioned open-world structure isn't much to write home about. excepting the seamless transition for this series (so yknow, removing loading screens), it's utterly standard for what AAA games have laid out so far: Giant Map, Collectibles, Safe Houses, Fast-Travel, Spend Three Minutes Driving To The Fun Bits. i haven't played Far Cry guys honest.

what's a bit more of a letdown is the new setting's blandness, partially due to the open-world structure smudging it all together. Kairos, this game's new planet, foregoes 3's cavalcade of zany space locations and instead returns to the wild wasteland look of Pandora, yet hews so closely that 4 has no visual identity of its own. i've seen these junkyard towns and juxtaposing futuristic military bunkers before, at least the previous game constantly threw new visual ideas at the wall. that 4's combat is so ludicrously satisfying as to keep my interest afloat through this is a testament to the series' unparalleled looter-shooter gameplay. i just wish it didn't throw the baby out with the bathwater regarding what 3 did right.

if you've never had an interest in Borderlands, BL4 likely won't convert you even with the surgical removal of its comedy. it is, largely, Yet More Borderlands, with changes that serve more as discussion fodder for those already invested in the loot-shoot-grind than anybody else. speaking as a longtime player though, BL4 frustrates me as a simultaneous continued improvement on what Borderlands does better than any other - the shooty - and an unnecessarily aggressive and misguided response to what Borderlands does poorly - the rest of it. thus, despite the differences, this is still Yet More Borderlands: take it or leave it.

[b]ULTRA-MEGA-CON:[/b]

It was 9 PM. My partner said he was tired.

I said: [b]"Come on, please, let's just do this one side quest. You can get a Legendary weapon from it, that sounds really cool!"[/b]

So my friend and I set off to find the legendary vending machine during the [b]"Vend of the Line"[/b] quest, and we're having a great time.

My partner has needed to [i]pee[/i] for quite a while at this point, but he's holding it in.

And then in the end...

Oh, what do I see?

I'm serious. I mean it. I'm getting sick of it. She's died like THREE TIMES

She's not a valuable character anymore. She doesn't need to be the center of every game. I get it, she's hot. That isn't enough from a story perspective to make characters thirst for her approval and shoehorn her into every game. Look, there was a time in the franchise where having her be the center of attention was not just tolerable, but a good decision. Her story should've ended in three at the latest. 
Guys, you can make more sirens. You have an in-universe explanation on how to make that happen. You don't even have to kill her off, you can have her retire to a distant moon and supplement the new sirens with the deaths of others. You have plenty of room to make it work. You could even make it a big deal when she does eventually die and have a dlc where we attend her funeral and experience the birth of another siren and have adventures in her moon fortress and console her hot lesbian wife (or husband, whatever). 

Back on topic, the characters are bland and tasteless. The only one that's interesting is zane, and it's exclusively because he's annoying. All the other NPCs feel like they were slapped together for the sake of plot progression. Somehow they even made claptrap suck. Interacting with him feels less like the kind of chore you want to do because wacky hijinks might ensue and more like the kind of chore you do to push yourself closer to being able to say you've completed the story and you're done with the game. 

Let's talk about inventory management.

Borderlands has always had a sort of quirky inventory system that is developed to feel like it's running on scavanged tech that's held together with duct tape and bandit tears. The echo 3 was a perfect example. It's premium because despite being a bootleg, the people building them are also using them, so they wanted to have fun with it.

The new system is a high tech robot that seems to only exist on this prison planet. It also seems to be the only one in existence, despite there being frames available. I'm sure there's a plot reason for this, but I don't care enough to look into it because it has no charm whatsoever. It feels like it's there just because it has to be, not because anybody actually cares enough to use one. The neck-implanted suppression devices could've accomplished literally everything the echo does. It would even have been more interesting, because you could've said that some team of imprisoned software developers rooted the thing and built an interface that was botched but functional. You could've had progression upgrades based on the idea that this team built a new patch, and you even could've had an Easter egg where you find them in a bunker somewhere. 

The storyline feels forced. It doesn't remotely feel interesting enough to keep you coming back. I forced myself to slog through it because I'm a fan of the franchise.

Also, when borderlands 3 ended, we were in a ship heading off to explore other vaults right? Did we just decide that was it? Did the ship crash? Like that's super anticlimactic. I was really hoping for bl4 to pick up on the ship, getting picked up as one of the new characters like some interplanetary hitch-hiker. Thing is, if the ship did crash in bl4, (which would explain a lot) then where are the rest of the characters from 3? Honestly, why kill off a ship travel system that players generally liked for a sub-par story with poorly chosen NPCs and bad gunplay? What gain is there to be had? What possible direction can we go from here?

Here's the thing. I love borderlands. I always have, and I always will. It's more than a sunken cost fallacy, it's nostalgia pure and simple. I critique this game not because I want to hate it, but because I want to love it. I want to see gearbox do with borderlands 4 what they did with 3. I don't expect a perfect game, I can never expect anything remotely close to 1 or 2. I just want something fun to play in the universe I've come to love. I understand it's difficult, it has to be. Something like this wouldn't be the case if it was easy to make a good borderlands game. But for the price we're all paying, I feel like we should be able to expect a bit more y'know?

I think I actually enjoyed BL3 a bit more. While the characterization of the siblings wasn't great, the streamer persona specfiically they had some really interesting dynamics between themselves and their father. BL4's villains are kinda just there. Like Zol was a nothing burger, just an idiot trying to get the time keeper to look his way. Vile Lictor did some interesting stuff with trying to become a siren, but he dies before anything meaningful could be done, and the ripper queen Callis was even more of a nothing burger than Zol. You actually fight her twice and the 2nd fight made literally no sense to me. How did she get there, why was she there, did I miss a line of dialogue or something? The time keeper also does not have *any* staying power, partially because he barely ever interacts with you, and once he starts to become a bit interesting he's dead. I don't really get why gearbox struggles so much with villains. The npcs in this game are also quite a bit worse than the prior games but that is mainly because of the open world nature of the game. I really enjoyed Zane and Levaine, but they are only present for the last 3rd of the game. Zane and Amara are also great but they are both from BL3 which makes sense as my favorite parts of BL3 were the BL2 characters. The muscle bro is just a worse version of Brock, far too wholesome for borderlands imo, and Calder is probably the best mix but he is only there for 1/3 of the game. I think the open world nature of this game has some benefits, but I actually think Borderlands needs to be more linear for borderlands style storytelling to work. The world can't change when you have to be able to go back and access every part of it. I think a good middleground would be a well made hub area and then linear paths and dungeons that you have to complete for the story. When you leave Kairos to go to Elpis the game's narrative quality all of the sudden shoots up, you can feel Amara's desperation to save Lilith and even Zane becomes more endearing as they both feel connected to Lilith because of BL3. The game, sadly, really shines only in the linear sections as the pacing finally makes sense. The little respite after saving Lilith and killing Callis (for the 2nd time) is really what I crave from Borderlands and BL4 simply doesn't have enough of it due to it's open world structure. Also, after your first fight with Callis the game becomes way more linear and, imo, becomes way better. What a confusing game.

There are some good changes in this game though, legendaries are more rare than in bl3 which makes getting them while leveling feel good, same with pearlescent drops. The ability to heal was actually really fun and allows for much more aggressive gameplay when you roll a good medstim. The game further dipping it's toes into diablo and poe style item drops is great, there is so much more build variety now with items getting random rolls and parts, albeit at the cost of gun manufacturer identity. Being able to summon a sparrow like Destiny was great, but that is necessary for an open world style game.

I really hope gearbox doesn't give up on Borderlands, the series has meandered since BL2 but I know it can hit its stride if it just decides on what it wants to be. Currently, it can't decide between a destiny style looter shooter experience, a call of duty style linear narrative experience, or a breath of the wild style open world sandbox. I think all three of these can exist in a single game but it is up to gearbox to combine them all into a satisfying experience as currently Borderlands has an Identity problem.

I have genuinely tried hard to give Borderlands 4 a fair chance and find things to love, but coming straight from Borderlands 3, it feels like a downgrade in almost every single way, starting right down to the engine shift. Shockingly, moving to Unreal Engine 5 is a massive downgrade because not only does it make the game run worse, but they leaned way too hard into fancy lighting and graphical choices that make the overall image look muddy while completely stripping away the franchise's iconic comic-book charm. That visual mess bleeds into the weapon design too, where the new parts mechanic makes too many guns feel identical and uninspired, and far too many weapons rely on charge mechanics that bog down the pacing and make the gunplay feel sluggish instead of punchy. Exploration suffers just as much because, while the open world is massive, it is largely plain and empty. Biomes like the snow region and the desert might have different color palettes, but the actual traversal, activities, and enemy encounters remain completely repetitive and samey. The issue with repetition goes even further when you realize how much worse the enemy variety is here compared to previous games; you are stuck fighting the same few basic enemies across every single biome, which completely kills the pacing. Even the soundtrack takes a hit, trading the distinct region-specific music of past entries for the exact same songs playing on a loop during every single fight. The shift to a sprawling open world also completely ruined the tight, creative arena design that made previous entries shine, leaving combat spaces far too wide, open, and barren for memorable firefights. Furthermore, the vehicle system has lost all of its personality; Borderlands 3 nailed vehicle hunting by letting players track down distinct types with meaningful upgrades, but part 4 boils cars down to repetitive skins and invisible stat increases. Even worse, the new summon mechanic guts the classic atmosphere by ditching the Catch-a-Ride network and losing persistent vehicle placement, removing a layer of immersion that used to make the world feel lived-in and real. To top it all off, the endgame content is vastly inferior to what 3 offered, and while some might excuse it by saying the game is still new, looking at the actual speed and scale of what is being added proves otherwise. The post-launch DLC adds a meager couple of hours of gameplay, whereas past expansions easily delivered ten hours or more of rich content per drop.

I've played Borderlands games since Borderland 1. While I consider B2 an absolute masterclass in the balance of story-telling, gameplay, replay value, loot management, humor, and badassery, this game has now taken it's rightful place as my second favorite Borderlands installation. I was [b] extremely [/b] skeptical that this game would be a halfway decent entry into the series as Borderlands 3 was my least favorite game and honestly got less than 30 hours of play from me across systems. As soon I started playing THIS game however, I was hooked! I think the game can be broken down into several major points of success:

[h3] Story [/h3]I was immediately pissed off by the Timekeeper the instant I interacted with him. Not in the same way I was with the Calypso twins. Nono, they made me angry in the cheapest and most annoying way possible. The guy however, I wanted to rip his throat out in all the same ways I wanted to with Handsome Jack. While I personally prefer the humor of Jack, this guy was a temptation, always staying out of reach and making me feel like I had something to prove. Progressing through the map, tackling the story, I was pleasantly surprised by how well the story and exploration complimented each other, which bring me to my second point...

[h3] Completion [/h3]As someone who plays through every side quest and seeks to collect every legendary, I was SO HAPPY at the routes the game took me for quests. I felt like every time I completed a mission I was exploring a brand new place. I know these games are infamous for running you back and fourth between points for simple objectives, but WOW the devs KILLED it with location in this game. And that map is enormous, like it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HUGE. I sunk 120 hours into my first playthrough happily and was completing each section of the map as I went. Completion was as satisfying, if not more so, than Borderlands 2. What an amazing job.

[h3] Guns & Gameplay [/h3]I mean, it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Borderlands, if you ♥♥♥♥ up the guns then you're doing something wrong. Not much to say here other than gameplay was familiar but fresh in all the right ways. I still don't care for sliding, but that's the case in every game I play.

[h3] Graphics [/h3]Holy ♥♥♥♥ the graphics are stellar. I mean it takes a spaceship to even boot the game, but when you do you are in for a treat. The reflections in blood splats, the shadows and global illumination, the strange parallax between distant parts of the map and close buildings is so cool. You feel like every part of the world is it's own place that's been designed to be small, yet you can literally walk from one side of the map to the other without ever having a black loading screen. The way the team blended the outlined Borderlands style with modern shading techniques is nothing short of masterful. Everything looks amazing and I'm a graphics slut so this is a big win in my book.

Overall, if you like borderlands (especially Borderlands 2) and are wanting a new true-to-form installation of the series, this is it. I think the only thing I could wish for is more replay value in the endgame and more DLC for the game, but even then I still have so much content o go with what's already been released. 10/10

Let's get this out of the way early: The "millennial writing" dialog from BL3 is, effectively, gone.  BL4 is something of a course correction in storytelling and world-building. Don't take that too far, though, this game never rises to the level of the story set by BL2 (but it's acceptable). Even thinking about that BL3 story makes me a bit irritated. Anyway, moving on...

As for the gameplay, it's solid and even feels great at times (moment to moment). The guns are the best part (as usual) and you can expect a ton of variations in the weapons. The different classes of Vault Hunters offer a lot of replayability if that's your thing. The world design is "open world" and it's OK, for the most part. There are a few segments of the map that are purposely designed to be a pain to navigate. I don't know why map / world designers insist on that, but most of the map is perfectly acceptable.

The biggest problem with the game, by far, is the shader compilation. I have never seen a game that take 10-20 minutes to compile shaders ONLY TO MAKE YOU COMPILE THEM AGAIN ON THE WORLD MAP. What in the actual frak is going on there? The entire point of compiling shaders when the game boots is to avoid shader compiling during general gameplay.
Only buy the game if it is on severe discount. Otherwise you are better off playing BL3.

Generally, if you like BL3 or Tiny Tina's, and you want more of that you'll like this. If you thought that BL3 had too much story & personality youre in luck! BL4 has way less of both. If you just want to punch the gun box over and over again, BL4 is another chance to do that! In broad strokes, BL4 is an excellent, perhaps even top tier FPS entry. The combat has all the pieces. Each of the 3 major factions (and many sub factions) have very unique enemy types and interactions which keep every combat arena fresh. This is doubly true of places where the factions interact and where you can get 3 or 4 way battles. This gels well with the loot you get, which gives you tools to pick apart groups of enemies and beat them down. There is a story here, some cool moments and good vibes, and if you found the story of BL3 annoying (many did) this tones it down from 11 to 8 or 9. And as a coop game, its super fun. I've actually done most of my playtime in coop and have enjoyed it. 

But in the details the game falls apart. Its buggy as hell. The breadcrumb trail to missions is often drunk and breaks super easily. I've had bosses glitch out and just stand there till I delete them. Enemies will fall through the world, or get stuck behind terrain, or just not load in any AI behaviors and stand by their spawn doors. This can be SUPER annoying when you have to kill enemies to progress, maybe half the time this ends with you hunting for the one bad guy whose AI broke. One specific propaganda tower (side mission type) cant be completed for me because it gets stuck at 75%. Maybe an enemy is breaking, maybe the quest. I've had missions not play story audio. Sometimes things just happen and I have to ask 'is this intended behavior, am I not getting the puzzle, or is the game just broken.' And usually its about 1/3rd to each, which is too much. But when it works, boy it works. The combat can be very tactical. The combination of abilities, grenades, and gunplay can be quite satisfying. When the music hits, youre bouncing around the arena, and everything is working right, the game is a solid 9/10.

Beyond this the game is just, IDK, pointless. There hasn't been a lot of change in the BL formula in the last decade, and its really starting to strain against core design limitations. On my current char I have $100m space bucks. Because I can't spend it, because vendor loot is 99% useless. I only spend cash when I die, I never buy new guns. But if I don't need money why I am picking up any loot at any point? The only loot that matters *at all* is the loot that makes your numbers bigger. But enemies scale to your char lvl, so getting better loot just gives you a chance to jump the power curve. But many enemies are designed to be overpowered at your level, there are lots of tanky enemies and oneshot/high DPS baddies going around. So you never really make much progress or get truly OP. As long as your not UP, does the loot really even matter then? Most of it doesn't impact how you play at all. Thats bad when the selling feature is 'lots of guns to loot.' Past the starter quests, 90% of loot I get is not at all useful for my class. But not only is loot a core selling feature, getting a spin on the loot wheel is the primary reward to any activity. And its kinda pointless. Even worse, unlike in most FPS where you get a feel for guns, you are getting so much loot and swapping so often you keep a good gun for, maybe, 20 min before you drop it for a new gun with a bigger number. Do you hate the new fire mode (like the Order charge rifles, which are horrid)? Too bad! Does it not jive with your build? Maybe the next will! Who cares! None of it matters. Just make the number bigger. Nothing is permanent, nothing matters, nothing sticks with you. What the game needs is the freedom for me to rebuild my own guns, but they cant do this because the battlepass is selling you premium legendaries and anyway modifying anything serious with your guns just further breaks the loot wheel. So, like, what exactly is the point of all this? Beyond this combat can be vomitous, at at higher levels some enemies just melt you. But in a game with lots of abilities, interactions, enemy types, you need to prioritize or you need to mag dump. When combat  encounters become unreadable, you cant snipe or burst down baddies all you can do is pop your ult and unload. But, again, this betrays the core of what the game should be, you cant be a static player with so man DOT regions, and low ROF weapons have a way smaller niche than high ROF esp when aiming gets messy.

 Oh and the class skill tooltips are badly written to the point that its impossible to know how to build characters. What does "+6% kill skill effectiveness" actually mean? Who knows, BL doesnt seem to. Worse still, the shooting controls are horrid on a controller. This was a problem Halo 1 solved in 2001, but here IDK whats off but its one of the worst feeling shooters I've played in a decade and no amount of settings changes seem to fix that. Because shooting feels so bad, you really just want to spray and pray from the hip. What, you keep getting purple sniper rifles? 

Thankfully the story is ALSO bad. Or, flat, more specifically. Because of how poorly the Twins in BL3 were received,  every character in BL4 is now very safe, generic, and flat. Personality and edges were sanded down, and the game is just a wet fart in terms of content. There are cool moments, nice set pieces, hype moments, but it never goes anywhere or does anything with it. Gearbox and do some cool DBZ style action direction, but like the gun wheel you just see it and move on. The side content varies from bizarre and surreal to sad, experimental, existential, etc. Some of that content, like 'The Boss' storyline where you help a gangster get his, is pretty fun. All of this is cut out at the knees with some really aggressive millennial toilet humor. If youve never played BL, its Marvel humor with more cursing and poop jokes. And if you hated it in BL3, its still here in BL4. Is it funny when I shoot the ripper and they shout 'agh, hamburgers!'? Sometimes, but there is so much of it that doesnt land. 

So do I recommend BL4? No. If you havn't beaten BL3 I don't think BL4 is worth playing, not because you MUST KNOW THE STORY, but because BL3 is more stable, the same gameplay, and you can get way cheaper. There is nothing in BL4 that matters, or is worth caring about, outside of the combat balance & class building. Which is either the same or better in the older, cheaper titles. The sole use case for this game, IMHO, is you want a good coop game with a buddy. I have put a ton of time into this so far, but most nights I end up feeling like I'd rather have played Darktide or some other coop experience.

If there was a "kind of" button instead of a flat yes or no, that would be the one I'd push. For the tl;dr version, I'd say this is a yes, but only kind of.

Does it satisfy a little bit of that borderlands nostalgia? Yes. 

Was it fun to play through the first time and dork with builds and guns and bosses and all the extra open world content they built in? Kind of, but the way it was built didn't leave me feeling like I needed to explore everything. The keys to the kingdom were highlighted nice and neat, and even when a collectible wasn't highlighted you can take one of the air jump things and tell exactly where collectibles would be. They built an open world game and didn't incentivize exploration, and that blew my mind.

Did I personally have performance issues? Initially, yes, but I found a combo of settings that made it run nearly seamlessly on my middle tier PC (3060ti, 8gb ram, blah blah).

Does it have that replay-ability that made me keep coming back to BL3 on both PC and Playstation? Well, I thought I'd come back to it when the first story pack addition dropped with the new VH and...I haven't. The only reason I'm writing this is because I had an itch to play Borderlands and saw this one sitting there in my library. The game itself is fun if you like turn-your-brain-off-and-click type of looter shooters. I switched guns very rarely because nothing packed quite the punch that the ones I had equipped did. Pretty sure I beat the game with mid-level guns. It all boils down to what other people have said: It's missing...something. The entire map is handed to you, with identifiers highlighting where you should look for most of it. The zone collection challenges don't feel rewarding when you get a green to vendor immediately. The zone transitions were the only thing that was rough on my PC (not area, but zone) but it still managed. I can see what they tried to do, but they didn't quite hit the mark. 

Still marking this as a recommend, because I was able to get 80ish hours out of it before beating it, but there's really not anything calling me back to it after beating it like in the previous installments. Just a bunch of "fast travel here and kill this thing. Then fast travel there and kill this thing" for an incredibly small chance at upgrading any gear. BL3 (unpopular opinion, but it's my favorite) had entirely different WORLDS to explore and so much to interact with. This game feels pretty empty. It's either roads to the next area that's highlighted on your map, or a set of 3 beasties to kill in a random place.
