I have to talk about performance because, honestly, it could have been a lot better.

When I first played through Borderlands 4, I had some fun... if the performance allowed it.

Story

The Vault Hunters are fun. The story has lots of new characters, some more interesting than others. Some returning characters from previous entries also make a comeback.

When it comes to the villain, I wasn't impressed, but it was at least a step up from the villains in Borderlands 3. (I hated them in a bad way.)

The pacing could have been better. Maybe this only holds true for me, but... I could not bring myself to care about most of the new characters, mainly because a lot of them felt very one-note.

Most bosses were... meh, in my opinion. They tried to be creative here and there, with things like crystals you need to shoot, but none of them really blew me away.

Gameplay

The guns feel great. Finally, snipers feel like snipers again. The combat is also very fluid (when the game's poor optimization allows it).

However, I've played through the game twice, and I can say this: if you get bored fighting the same enemies over and over again, you'll get bored fast in Kairos.

The Vault Hunters have some cool, unique powers and feel different from one another, which I really enjoyed.

The Map

In my opinion, this is one of the two weakest links in the game so far.

I love that they tried something new with an open-world Borderlands, but the world feels empty and pointless at times. The repetitive enemies don't help in this regard either.

I would much rather have a smaller map with more intentional map design that feels well thought out.

The Second Weak Link: Atmosphere

The atmosphere in this game is, for me, a huge miss.

The game wants to make you feel like a chosen action hero so badly that it ruins the experience for me.

The older games, like Borderlands 2, made me feel like I was a survivor trying to survive the harsh life on Pandora while also trying to defeat the overarching villain, Handsome Jack.

Borderlands 2 felt serious and silly at the right times.

The music this time around really doesn't feel like Borderlands to me either. The older games had more of a lone-survivor vibe. For example, I really miss the lone guitar strings from Borderlands 2.

Legendary Drops...

I hate this game's abundance of legendary drops.

It's not nearly as bad as the drop rate at launch in Borderlands 3 but still.

I miss when legendaries were LEGENDARY. Getting one used to feel like winning the lottery. Now you can hop on the game, wait five minutes for the shaders to compile, and finally get to playing... only to get a legendary two minutes later from killing some random fodder enemy.

That being said, Borderlands 4 is not a bad game. It could have been a lot better.

Overall, I had fun with it, but there are quite a few things holding it back from being a truly great Borderlands game.

This is the first borderlands game I haven't liked.  The world is far too large with too much walking to progress the story.  You have to walk for ages to get your first vehicle to make the first area even manageable.  I also, can't really describe this, but everything seems smaller.  Smaller icons, larger POV making things smaller, smaller text, etc.  But my biggest gripe is how they revamped the inventory experience.  For borderlands 2, 3, pre sequel, you could see what you had equipped alongside your gear in the backpack, so you didn't have to really do much to compare.  You could scroll through your inventory and see what you have pretty easy.  The new menu separates these apart and makes a classic gear heavy game even more cumbersome to manage. If you love to memorize things or test your memory, this won't be an issue for you.  To me I find it annoying.  Normally I have fun with these games within the first hour.  4 hours into this....I just feel like, its boring and annoying.  I did the Rafa vault hunter and maybe that is why?

I wanted to update my review because I am 1) glad I got a reach out from the developer, which, shows a genuine effort to do better and 2) I wasn't very clear on the "smaller" piece I was talking about.  Again, my main gripe is the inventory. The icons for the backpack and inventory are ridiculously small.  I know they made it into a massive tiled map of equipment, which, and this is just my personal preference, hurts the game.  Borderlands is known for its unique guns, and in older BL games, I could just memorize the look because they were so distinctive.  But now, the icons are like 1 inch by 1 inch.  They have these beautiful weapons but trivialize them by shrinking their choice within the menu to be too small.  Also, personal preference, I hate how modern UI design favors left to right scrolling vs up and down.  It was what I loved about the original borderlands.  I don't like going through a list left to right, I don't know who does.  The original menuing was vertical which, again maybe just me, seemed far easier to understand who was better than whom. It just isn't fun, I don't even know why. BL1 is nostalgic, BL2 is a masterpiece, BL3 is great, but didn't live up to the standard set by 2, and Borderlands 4 is just kinda there. This is a case of an open world game that just feels empty. 

The guns are all "quirky", but rather than it being in a fun way like they were in 3, they're just annoying to use. 

I haven't run into any performance issues, other than the game needing to compile shaders every time I fast travel, die, etc.

The bosses and other characters were so lackluster that by the time I made it to the end-game I was just too sick of it to play it anymore. The main allies and enemies aren't memorable at all. Maybe I rushed through the main story too fast or something, but I did that on 3 and could still at least remember their names a week after playing it. Not to mention, ya know, actually wanting to play it again that next week.

The movement, double jump, jetpack, and grappling hook feel fun to use, but they don't make up for how channelized the map is. You'll either get yourself into an area that has no way out other than jumping into a bottomless pit, or you'll spend 5 minutes trying to find the right path to the next quest marker.

It feels like they were expecting the open world to be the big show-stopper addition, and put no work into making it feel alive or fresh. Any enemy encampment is either a monster nest, futuristic base/outpost, or raider shanty town that you've seen in the last 3 main games. All packed with enemies that are just kinda spongy and more of a pain to fight rather than enjoyable.


TL;DR
Pick it up on a steep discount if you're a fan of the franchise. In it's current state, It's worth about 30 dollars in my opinion, not 70. Performance issues aside, it feels unfinished. There are early access games that have more life and care put into them than this.

It took a while to decide if I wanted to recommend this one or not. My decision was perched on the edge. On one hand, I had many many great hours in Borderland games. The first few were some of my favorite FPS's. This game was quintessentially Borderlands... at least in overall gameplay. But that's not all in it's favor. After 4 main games, many DLC, and one Tiny Tina fever dream, the gameplay is stale. Some changes were made to Borderlands 4, but not enough to bring back the spark. It was still fun, just not inventive or challenging. Many of the challenges were more annoying than anything, and the gameplay got boring really fast. 

The story was terrible. The basic elements were there, but it just didn't go anywhere. It was a rehashing of earlier stories, with very little to show for it, and almost no depth to the characters. Even Claptrap was barely his annoying, persistant self. Sure, he had some lines and sent you on some tasks at the start but even then. And for those of you who go "well that actually sounds like a relief" (and I don't blame you), it felt more like hollow fan service than a reintroduction of a... barely tolerab... I mean, beloved character. The same goes for Lilith and the other callbacks. A few lines, but no personality. Very little of the old humor too. 

Finally there are the graphical issues. I'm running this on CachyOS with Proton, but I have 32GB DDR5 RAM, a Nvidia 4080 Super, and an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D. You'd think it be a breeze to run this game, but it's not. DLSS sucked so bad. Without DLSS I was only able to keep it at 60, but with random drops and my framerate utterly died in the wide open areas. There's some graphical issue with the borderlines that made DLSS impossible to use, so I went with TSR. I finally got it running above 60FPS on the second highest setting, but it still had trouble with wide open areas and some stuttering. 

So if you've enjoyed borderlands overall and want to enjoy old gameplay in a new setting, I'd say toss this into your wishlist and wait for it to drop below $15. Otherwise go find something else to spend money on.

Cons:

 * The loot system is abysmal. You are level 5 in the game (meaning very early on) you kill one mob 8 weapons drop, There are 5 chests around you each has 6 more guns. Since there is so much stuff, I feel like common and uncommon at least instantly feel irrelevant - so they might as well not exist. The people having issues with crashing and shaders is something i cannot say I've experienced. Borderlands 2 was mediocre feeling gunplay held up with a fun gameplay loop, great character archetypes and a carrot-on-a-stick loot chase that was addictive. since then, each title has gotten better at the general gunplay and mechanics. That being said, the pull of endgame content and wanting to chase legendary drops DOES exist. But it doesn't match the series' previous highs. Love this game despite all of it's flaws. Although I recommend waiting for a sale to get the game, just like any other borderlands title.

The obvious drawbacks to this game are performance. It's not great, especially on lower end machines and falls victim to a lot of the poor optimizations that come with a game running UE5 as the engine. However, I will say, the game performs a lot better than I remember on launch and there's some tricks to help boost performance and keep it consistent. Overall, on my machine it runs decently okay, but results may vary 

Open world somewhat works for this game, it just feels like they didn't do enough with it. The only real reason to do a lot of the content in the world is for SDU tokens and opening up bosses. There's no real other reason to complete a lot of this content, especially on replays. Kinda wish they would've stuck to the more open-level design they used in previous games. 

Story is decent, bosses feel good to fight against and are pretty well done in this game. Although, late game or even early game if you know what you're doing, the bosses can be taken down really quickly / one shot. Farming in this game is pretty good to especially with the introduction with the Moxxi's Big Encore Machine. 

Late game, the game is struggling a bit for content. As of writing this, there are 4 single-mission bounty packs which each have a couple of bosses and new loot. Each one takes about an hour, hour and a half or so to complete. Then there's the Mad Ellie DLC which so far looks like it's going to take me about 4-5 hours to fully complete. Besides that, the currently Two Raid Bosses and the Takedown, there's not too much in the way of end game content, which is a shame. I genuinely hope they add more Takedowns as that is by far my favorite end-game content added so far. 

Personally my favorite part of the game is the Phosphene (Shiny) Legendary hunting. I enjoy grinding for super rare stuff and these super rare skins for the Legendary weapons are fun to grind for. 

Overall, I'd give the game a solid 7/10. TL;DR the game needs a lot of work for the End-game content, performance issues can vary and the open world needs some work. But it's a pretty solid game despite all of those flaws.

This one is a rough review. I like Borderlands, I like borderlands a LOT. In fact, I like it so much I've bought the handsome collection (1, 2, and pre-sequel) 3 times, borderlands 2 and its dlc twice, the tales games, and this game. I even 100 precented borderlands pre-sequel, and 3 plus dlcs. On the surface, this game had things going on about it that made me rather excited for it when the trailers were coming out. The vault hunters looked cool (after their re-design) and had nice little abilities and lore tid-bits, the villain was NOT another handsome jack clone, expy, or wannabe and there was even... a villain vs villain war going on? How cool! And then it was revealed the game was not only going to be running using Unreal Engine 5 (uh oh) but that it was going to be open world (ah ♥♥♥♥). And that immediately had me worried, because I had just been burned my Monster Hunter Wilds going down the same route, and Metroid Prime, and... alot of games this year actually. Open world has been THE plague of 2026 gaming. But it came out, and the stupid little launch trailer did me in so I forked over 70 USD for the base game. And the game *looks* nice, sort of. The writing is better than base game BL3 (which is... practically an insult with how low that bar was.) and the setting itself is rather interesting. A planet that ALSO had Elpis as a moon that was cloaked by the Timekeeper as a sort of safe haven, until the mayhem caused by it's ugly neighbor Pandora and its' denizens cause the moon to explode... twice and shatter the sky. The time keeper goes nuts and implants people with bolts that control them in any which way the timekeeper wants, and ripping it out causes you to go crazy and become this game's version of a bandit. The two factions don't like eachother, as the Order sees the Rippers as ♥♥♥♥♥ up maniacs, and the Rippers don't like the Order's sterile and boring way of life. This is cool, there is a groundwork for things to be done here... 

Except it's then revealed that the time keeper can only be accessed by 3 "command bolts", which can only be obtained from his 3 lieutenants... one of which is the leader of the Rippers and a Turncoat. Which means the game works like Far Cry 5 and 6 now. And that entire civil war thing is wasted, now. Hell, any time a ripper force and an order force do fight, they'll stop and kill you if you get too close. So, this whole thing is a bust, but how does the game work now that the most interesting thing in terms of it's premise is a bust? 

Well, it doesn't. Or at least, not well. The game breaks, all of the time. And the things that DO work, work POORLY and oftentimes just worse than they did in even Borderlands 2, a game that was 13 years old when this game released by the way. The map is confusing to navigate in the menu, because the in game map doesn't do layers. So if an objective is in a cave or ABOVE you, you won't find out until you are close enough for it to be a pain in the ass. And because navigation takes so much longer and is more confusing because the world is now open, you get a guideline. The guideline doesn't work. It can: Disappear early, Phase through terrain (including Mountains, Buildings, the FLOOR, and it can even sneak out of bounds), or even just not let you activate it. For no reason. Sometimes the game just does not let you use the guideline, even if you are not in a location that bans it. Or how about guns! Guns have parts! The guns in this series are actually just a bunch of parts SMASHED together which determines things like stats and manufacturer. Especially important in this game, where you can get guns with parts made by other manufacturers, including ones that aren't properly in the game. So, a Hyperion add-on adds the aim shield to your gun, a Jakobs barrel adds the crit ricochet, so on and so forth. So, in a game where knowing what parts do, how do you check on them? In borderlands 2, you inspect the gun in your inventory. In the pre-sequel, you inspect the gun in your inventory. In borderlands 3, you inspect the gun in your inventory. In borderlands 4? You can't. If the part is not important enough to show up on the info card (the one that tells you general stats and weapons manufacturer when you look at it on the floor or scroll over it in the menu), you do not get to see what a part does. Which is any manufacturer part that isn't a cross-manufacturer part or legendary. So, you just... don't have the same level of info as you do in a game that is now 13 years old and it feels bad. They also rarely mesh with your vault hunter skills in a way that matters, outside of buffing the status ailments or more stats. Vault hunter skills also sometimes just don't work. Okay, so what about the things that you use the guns on, enemies? Those should be fine, right? 

No. Enemies are very weird in this game. And not fun weird I mean, they just don't seem to function right. Some enemy weakpoints just don't seem to work properly with the hit box either being too big, or too small. They can get stuck on geometry, and, while this isn't a bug, the leveling system for them is very out of order. In one zone they'll be your level and 20 feet to the north they'll suddenly be 10 levels higher than you, and it is instant death. This is a looter game, you cannot cheese this out without a hyper specific build. This is a sacrifice for the open world, as is performance. 

This game runs terribly. I've seen malware wreak less havoc on people's pcs than this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. It recompiles shaders more often than a chainsmoker going out for a smoke break, it stutters, it lags, and while I don't have the BEST specs on the market, I'm attaching my specs to show that they can be considered "pretty damn good" by most standards. But also the game crashes. A lot. It's better with patches but it sill crashes a lot more than a game costing 70 US dollars for the base game should. And it happens more often with longer play sessions, like there is a memory leak or something. 

Quests also don't work properly. Flags can sometimes not trigger, dialogue can repeat itself multiple times, dialogue can sometimes just not happen at all, sometimes the game is convinced that you aren't actually at the right spot because it marked the correct spot to be some random spot about 100 meters from where you are supposed to go. 

I haven't bought any of the dlc, but the free one was a single mission and the others are... about as long, except for the vault hunter dlc. Which comes with a full story...? Which is about 3 hours of content, or so I'm told. Which doesn't seem like it's worth 40 usd. To be fair, I don't think you could convince me 40 usd is a worthwhile price on any dlc unless it's something like Icebourne or Sunbreak where it doubles the size of the game. Which this is not. But I don't know how those are gameplay wise, or story wise because like... they are so prohibitively expensive for what appears to be so little, so those might improve things. C4SH might actually be balanced properly. I don't know. 

But TL:DR, this game is a mess. It's buggy, and at times even broken. The UI sucks in ways that would be bad for a game released during the ps3 era, let alone in 2026. The story is fine, but has missed potential in exchange for basically being a Far Cry game. The map exploration sucks, because it's either tedious or unrewarding, and enemies and fighting CAN be fun! 


When they work. 
I'd wait until all of the dlc is out and they fix the game in order to convince dumbasses like me to buy the dlc and rave about how this game was secretly a misunderstood masterpiece, or at least actually a fun game. Like what happened with Borderlands 3, and to a lesser extent, Tiny Tina's wonderlands. Or get it on deep sale, if you can run it. Test your hardware.

I've played this game for about 60 hours, grinding side missions, collectibles, and slow playing the main story with friends. I got to about level 19, my game hard crashed, it corrupted my save, and I had to start over. Upsetting, but whatever, hopefully a fluke. Last night at level 57 the same thing happened and I can't recover my saves. 

This happens enough that there are forum posts all over for how to fix this. Navigate to game folder, rename some files, maybe download a 3rd party mod from Nexus, whatever. It's absolutely horsesh*t that all of these workarounds are necessary to maybe fix a corrupted save due to poor game coding.  

What I did experience is 40% of the older BL games with the other 60% being poor writing and and stupid amount of travel because the designed quests around running to places aren't easily accessible. It's monotonous and not rewarding. I bet of the 60 hours I've played, 15+ have been just running around either trying to find obscure entrances, running 5 miles between quest points just to run back, or trying to go 100 ft North, but there's a mountain, so I get to go all of the way around it. There aren't enough fast travel points, the map is huge, and it sucks to traverse.  

That actual game play is solid. Arguably the best game play in the series as far as gun options and the feel when fighting, but it's heavily outclassed by all of the negatives.  

I suppose if you like restarting your playthroughs because of Gearbox's awful design, dealing with a terrible antagonist, poor writing, and enjoy installing 3rd party tools to make it slightly more stable, then this is the game for you. If you don't like all of that, then don't waste the money on this trash pile, even if it's on super steam sale. You could manually backup you game saves, but I ask why is that necessary when there are cloud syncs? Terrible experience, and I actively recommend not buying this game at any price.

**Sigh**... As someone who looks at a borderlands game and thinks "That's something I wish I could experience for the first time again!" this game just doesn't really scratch that itch. I am glad that they kept with the pre-built vault hunters I think that system works really well and the skill trees had good build variety to them although balance is still always kind of an issue with one character usually being far superior but all others can still be fun and accomplish the whole game if you so choose. 

The open world. Well I thought this might be a good idea but it just turned out to be a detriment to the overall pace of the game. While it came with some quality of life things like purchasing respawns for bosses instead of saving and quitting every time you want to farm and random world events that have bosses who can drop legendary weapons it definitely comes with cons. Collectibles plague the map with some being annoying to get which are also tied to your inventory by the way which sucks, once you unlock fast travel it just becomes the same situation as any other borderlands game where you just travel where you want to go and don't bother driving around or running around anymore because there is just no reason to. 

Starting new characters is honestly just miserable. I don't know if they have fixed it since I stopped playing and I haven't bothered to go back and check but when you want to play another character everything is reset except your level that starts elevated, which doesn't even matter because all your storage is reset on weapons and backpack space and the map has all the fog of war again which requires you to run around and get all the map uncovered on each individual character. Don't know why they couldn't make the quality of life changes like those from day one since the game is all about grinding for shiny loot not hitting the same buildings over and over just to stop the map from harassing you with icons and lack of inventory spaces. 

The story is meh, forgettable just like 3. Although I will say that its going in a better direction than Borderlands 3, as I really hated the influencer storyline they attempted to create but that's neither here nor there. Some previous characters have returned while others are forgotten and I like that aspect but also dislike it due to lack of meaningful additions. For me a lot of the nostalgia was from the OG cast that made the game what it is with their quips and quirky personalities. Now the world is filled with mostly just bots that are unlikeable and quite honestly mostly annoying. 

Side quests are actually decently interesting which is a nice change of pace. Not all of them of course but enough to keep you wanting to find the next one here and there. Content overall is kind of dry, they don't have a complex system with the different tiers like they did in 3. They are adding more vault hunters and DLC so hopefully that can help this issue especially if they add more raid bosses and raids like they have on borderlands 3, I think that could potentially give more endgame replay ability here. But you will find yourself running out of meaningful things to do kind of quickly.

Unique loot is something this game really thrives off of and I really like their system here with changing out grenades for heavy weapons and throwing knives all with unique and fun effects if you want. Not to mention the legendary guns are a blast and fun to play with and break builds completely as usual. Obviously there is a meta and that is usually the go to, but its fun to mess around with some of the guns they have as they do neat things and its worth exploring what they can do or combine with to make some unique combinations or builds with. 

Lastly, performance. Anyone not under a rock knows this game is pretty badly optimized with crashes and the whole list of things you can mess up. I think a big contributing factor to this was the open world system, they just didn't know how to do it and optimize it well. Again I haven't played since a few months after launch, this could be fixed now or at least better than it was but beware that it probably won't run super well in general without serious settings tweaking. 

To summarize, I am a borderlands fan through and through. I bought the wallet snatcher edition because I wanted the whole experience and I love supporting these games. I think this sits in a neutral position for me but I want to lean more towards recommend just because of the history of these games and the overall fun you can have with friends. If you can snag this game on a sale definitely go for it, you'll get your hours worth, but as a fan this one hurts and I really hope this doesn't tank the series because it will be dearly missed if it does. Rating 6.5/10

It´s hard to make a Good/Bad list for this game becasue everything is a mixed bag.

The story and the Charackters are way more serious, unlike BL3 where it was only poop jokes left and right. Unfortunatly the Timekeeper is just hot air. While he is supposed to be the big bad guy who has the entire planet in a tight grip... He basically never does anything with it. I´m not going to go into more detail to not spoil to much if you still want to play it yourself. But I often asked myself: "Couldn´t he just kill everyone opposing him?" He could, but just doesn´t. The only reason he can´t control you is your echo-device. And you are the only person who has one.

The weapons feel like the variety is lower than ever befor. But why? Weapons can have licenses of other manufacturers. giving a jakobs weapon hyperion shields for example. But why does it feel so bad? Because nothing is uniqe anymore.
You can have a daedalus shotgun-with jakobs ricochet-that apply torgue stickys.
You can also have a jakobs shotgun-with torgue stickis- with the daedalus ammoswap.
While being different weapons they share the exact same gimmicks. 
Here is the problem:
The daedalus shotgun shots faster but deals less damage per shot - the jakobs shotgun deals more damage per shot but shoots slower.
There is no reason why you would ever want to use the daedalus over the jakobs therefore making the entire manufacturer irrelevant. 

The playable charackters, while being fun in manny ways, get overshadowed by a simple set of items (for the most part) Builds do matter for the endgame. and are irrelevant for everything else. for the entire main game all you need is:
1. a spreadlauncher attatchment on a jakobs shotgun
2. the amp feature on a revkit (and optionally the shield)
3. a crit knive
you will no oneshot every boss in game excluding raidbosses. No build required.

The open world is only a negative.
It´s mostly empty with only boring collectibles in it. It´s boring and there is nothing of substance to do. You only drive, drive, drive and drive in the probably worst vehicles the entire franchise has ever seen. (even the presequels cars where more usefull and fun)
Also the open world eats so much performance that it sometimes borderline unplayable, while only offering three visual styles. 
Green fields - desert - snowy mountain.  Everything looks the same.

Even 3 of the 4 bounty packs (that have released at the time of writing this) reuse these same assets.
The fourth one (A zane to kill for) is the best looking piece of content because of this.

The combat: I just have to say that i despise the fact that they have implemented modifiers into the basegame with no way to turn it off. Enemys create gravitiy wells on death or are randomly invisible or even invulernable, or shot balls at you that knock you around, and and and. It´s immersion breaking and annoying. 
One enemy type, the vile enemys, are additionally one of the most annoying enemys you could face. They have cristals all over their boddy that need to be destroyed, otherwise the enemy is fully immune to all damage, even if only a smal crystal remains. If they are broken they turn in to floating orbs that need to be destroyed again, otherwise they will just regreow, making the enemy immune once again.

Endgame... oh endgame...  It´s therrible.  The raidbosses are not fun. They share all the same terrible features stated above. But the worst out of all, the single reason why I cannot be asked to care at all about anny of them... Timers.
If you fight them in anny op lvl you are given a very strickt timer to kill them. If you fail you are locked out of uniqe legendarys. (wich also do not drop unless you are in a op lvl)
This invalidates 90% of all builds. You either play meta or fail.

A few side notes:
You can now replay missions from the quest menu. There is no reason to since you get no uniqe loot from missions AT ALL.
(in order to unlock the OP lvls you must replay missions with tedious modifiers)
You can respawn bosses without save-quitting. This is nice.
You can do a custom keybind that lets you supperjump. This is amazing.

I can genuinly NOT RECOMMEND this game.

... there are more stuff that I don't like. Had a lot of fun with the game, played with all characters (the addon one seems the worst), I like the arcade shooter feeling, dodging and moving around ... I just don't like the whole game and can't reccommend when even Borderlands 3 was better.

[h1]Borderlands 3, also known as "[i]Compiling Shaders: The Game[/i]"[/h1]

While it's less obnoxious and grating than three, and has fewer of the Mike Meyers-level attempts at non-American accents, it's still pretty dreary fare. 

Performance is mediocre, leaning heavily on upscaling and framegen, even on powerful machines. The actual game itself seems uninspired, throwing endless increasingly spongey trash mobs at you in huge numbers rather than doing anything distinct. Fiddly jumping puzzle? Here's a load of rubbish flying trash constantly battering into you. One of the endless lazy fetch quests? You're going to have to kill a lot of the same boring crap you've seen a thousand times before to get to Claptrap's left buttcheek or whatever you're after now. None of them will be fun or interesting to fight, it will just scale how much effort they take to kill. It feels like variety is not this game's strong suit.

Oh yes, Claptrap. Extremely grating, both the writing and the voicework feel like not the original people. It's so annoying that there's a dedicated volume slider to shut him up. Enough said.

It very much feels like the B-team were responsible for this. Even the famous generated Lego weapons are now an indistinct mass, due to the weird manufacturer mixing taking away their distinct identifies, much like the way that mixing plasticine too much always comes out poo brown. The effect of the famous cell-shaded graphics has been ruined by making many of the environments and their contents far too visually cluttered, so it just looks generic. It's like the current teams working on this don't really understand the game - which is probably the case, given the treadmill hire and fire in games now.

The upsides? As mentioned before, it's less obnoxious than BL3. Gone is the "hello fellow kids" edgelord dudebro  cringe "humour" - this is [i]extremely[/i] welcome. Now it's just a bit dull rather than life-threateningly awful. The game [b]REALLY[/b] needs dialogue skipping though, as literally none of it is consequential or worth listening to. CDPR these people are not.

It's quite buggy, especially during the (overpriced and skimpy) DLCs. Lots of mobs t-pose when killed, making it hard to see what's going on. Anything which triggers after you clear an area becomes a time-consuming slog because mobs fail to path around or clip into the scenery, so it takes ages and lots of fiddling to find and kill them.

I'm not sure that I recommend this game, having put far too many hours into it, trying to find the fun. If you do buy it, absolutely do not pay full price, wait for deep discounts. I bought it out of morbid curiousity, but it could well be the last BL game that I bother with.

TL;DR - it's less obnoxious than BL3 but it's still not good. Borderlands may effectively be over now.

Edit: Also, I got a "developer response" responding to the broad themes in the above within seconds of posting it, on a Sunday too - looks like Gearbox are using slop to be their Steam replyguy. Classy.

Borderlands 4 is a frustrating game, especially if you grew up on the first two entries. 

A main critique of Borderlands 3 was the poor writing. Which has been kind of improved here but not really. Certainly not for the price point. The dialogue has a tendency to sound like that "Quirky" dialogue popularized by newer age Marvel films and Netflix shows. Some of the dialogue has a tendency to sound so unnatural that its harder to listen to. It is not nearly as bad as 3 but we shouldn't be aiming for that. 

The change to the open world approach is odd to me. It's quite jarring. I guess my main issue with it is that it seems as though it was implemented to show off graphics in Unreal Engine 5 rather than actually tightening up the gameplay. Environments are cool when you first enter them but then get extremely tedious. It all looks the same. They also got rid of the radar and replaced it with a compass which was never asked for. They are very obviously trying to "modernize" Borderlands here and the whole thing just feels tasteless. 

They have added some movement stuff..because it can't be a new game without some sort of "Movement". There's a double jump, a dash, a ground pound and a BLATANTLY copied climbing mechanic from Apex Legends. I guess the changes are whatever. 

Shooting things, on the other hand, feels fantastic. Gunplay is tight as ever. However, even that can't really hold the game up. Every section so far for the main story so far is just you fighting waves and waves and waves of like 30 guys for 15 minutes at a time. There is very little weight or merit to the situations at hand. The main antagonist is quite cool, but you sort of "just want to get this done / get out of here" a LOT in this game. The dopamine hit from the first two entries in particular is gone. I'm not sure if it's a me thing or what, but the game feels sterile to me. It really does feel like they are attempting to cram as much crap happening on your screen as possible rather than creating calculated fights based on the plot like the second game. The customization with skill trees is cool as per usual and the Vault Hunters have cool abilities. But the issue here is that the gameplay is so dull that it's tougher to want to get through the whole tree. 

I'm not one to complain about performance in a review but honestly it falls apart for Borderlands 4 here. The game is playable on my hardware. However, getting 120 frames on a BORDERLANDS game with BORDERLANDS graphics is purely laughable. I don't even know how this can happen. It is mind boggling how poor development and optimization can be for mainstream FPS titles. 

Skip it until it is on a HEAVY discount. Or just go get Borderlands 2 and all of its DLC for like $10 on the next sale and have a better game. This is so painfully sub par. Flaccid, if you will.

Borderlands 4 is both a very hard and very easy game to discuss. In short, it is the best borderlands game. Period. I know we all love BL2, but I think we need to cope with the fact that that was lightning in a bottle. We aren’t getting a Handsome Jack 2 and the expectation that we might serves only to make all subsequent games harder to enjoy. 

Full disclosure, I don’t really care about endgame grinds or raid content. I’m here for the simple fun of playing the game.

The Good

The plot is great. It’s a huge step up from Borderlands 3 and the choice to partially reboot the narrative was long overdue. Actually, this is my soap box for a sec. People don’t care about Borderland’s plot. I mean, they do, but not in an active sense. BL2’s plot was a podcast you listened to as you played the game. It was great because it never got in the way. BL3 was a play you had to sit and watch.

BL3’s biggest issue was its pacing. It struggled because the game was broken into segments of high action, then no action. It got your heart pumping, then locked you in a room so it could tell you jokes. BL4 fixes it by never really locking you in a room. 

The shift has been a focus on player controlled pacing. Just wanna fart around and kill guys? No problem, go raid a base. Sick of action and want some down time? Pick up a sidequest and let people talk. Want to make progress? Do some story.  

BL3’s poor pacing made every other element of its story more frustrating. It wasn’t just that I found the kid annoying. It wasn’t just that characters had unearned emotional beats. It's that I was forced to sit and watch it happen. Doing away with that helped so much. 

The gun play is also massively stepped up. The game took elements from a bunch of other great FPS games, and smooshed them together and used it to reinforce the core loop. The hovering, dashing and grapplehook feel amazing. Turning grenades into ‘ordinances’ was a great decision and I love my throwing knives.

The skill trees are huge. Each character gets 3 trees, which themselves branch off into three sections. All the choices are interesting and there is a lot of room to fuddle-duddle and fiddle-faddle.

The Bad

The bad stuff about this game is where things get complex. I do not know how to evaluate an $160 AUD game. That’s a ludicrous price. Even 50% off, it still feels bad. This is especially hard to swallow knowing that the game will inevitably be discounted into the dirt.

The performance has apparently improved but the minimum requirements are still steep. Randy Pitchford’s response to players upset about that is also ridiculous. I’m playing the game on a six year old gaming laptop and given how much Cyberpunk 2077 I’ve played at 30-45 FPS, you have to understand that I can endure a bit of punishment. I grew up on second hand office PC’s. Playing like this feels nostalgic. 

That said, the high hardware requirements and excessive price of the game in an era where PC hardware is more expensive than ever means that Gearbox is asking a lot of players up front. I believe the experience is worth it even if the game looks like mud. But when Randy drops the advice to ‘simply spend thousands of dollars to play my game’. The level of tone-deaf cannot be overstated. I don’t blame people who won’t touch the game for it. 

This steep up-front cost is made all the harder to deal with given how hard it is to demo the game. The DRM on the game makes it impossible to “borrow” without a Hypervisor Bypass, which is scary for a lot of people. The game takes a full half an hour to initially compile its shaders (not to mention recompiling after adjusting your settings), which digs into your 2 hour refund window. The most intense sections of the game aren’t frontloaded, which means you might do fine for a second before your computer chugs. 

So is the game worth it? Idk. I’m having a great time and I’m keen to see what the grass looks like when I finally get a new PC. But I love Borderlands and could barely justify the game at 50% off. 

♥♥♥♥ Randy. I hope Gearbox and 2K unionise. Better contracts means better games.

Oh boy, Borderlands 4. Definitely one of those "in context" review.
I am going to put a positive recommendation mainly because right now it seat at "mixed" and considering what the value per euro it's kind of obscene. I got it for half of its (hefty) public price and yes, yes, it is a bland addictive fast food of a meal, but it's really a lot of big macs for the money. Even if you play just the campaign with most of the vanilla side quest that's 100h. Even full price that's 80c per hour wich few cool indie game compete with. It really is *not* a steal, you can see the production value, this game clearly took a lot of work.

Is it a good borderlands though? Depends I guess. Mechanically it's probably the best game although differences with the 3rd... didn't strike me that much? Of course it's all over the place and there is a huge variety in guns that's kind of something until you start legendary hunting and get weird OP guns that put everything else the game has to offer in the dust, often trivializing the game. Maybe it's because I am a veteran who knows that you die way more in this game from exploding barrels and your own grenades than anything else but the game was really too easy for me until I attempted to solo the end game content which ended up not being possible, big disappointment. The mobility is a big improvement in fight though, IMO it's done pretty well. Vehicles are a bit better to use etc.

It has the best headshot noise in any game, it's pornographic, so satisfying. Lack of midgets to headshot though (IYKYK) but interesting  opposition - the studio is really good at making a set of enemies with unique animations and game mechanics. Clearly a strong point.

The writing? Well it's probably on par or better than Borderland 1. I never smiled but I was never irked. Some characters have at least some lasting powers. The bad guy is bland AF. It's just your inoffensive story for a game that had amazing writing in one of their game (Borderlands 2) by accident. One thing it does better than any other game though is your own character's writing, at least Rafa. It has to be the first time I actually acknowledged and liked my character in a Borderlands game. Which is a huge feat, it has to be said.

The problem is that the writing in the 3 was so bad we didn't notice another glaring it had that aslo cripples Borderlands 4 because no one yelled about it to Gear box back then. 

The disappearance of any atmosphere. Of any mood.

Some say it's Jasper Kid being gone but I don't think it's that or only that. At some points the soundtrack can even run its old gimmicks pretty well. The real issue started when we left Pandora. IMO one of they key common quality of all good open world FPS is that they induce melancholy somewhere past the 20h mark. STALKER, Fallout... not Farcry :P 

You go in a state where you connect to the game space in a deep way, navigating from this feeling of melancholy induced by the world, the mood to the dopamine of killing and looting. Borderlands 1 and 2 had it because Pandora is a perfect stage for that. It's desperate, derelict place. I remember in the first one in the DLC, there was a hub at some kind of "end of the world" which was just breath taking. Borderlands 2 introduced greenery but it still worked because it was this one obscene contrast with the rest of the world. Then Borderlands 3 went "all the landscape", which immediately meant "none of them". Nothing meant anything.

In Borderlands 4 the act 1 (which will last you 30h if you do side quests) is some wow like bland greenery. It has zero mood. It's really a sad thing. The rest of the map is way better but even if it at times look stunning, it never gets melancholic. It feels just like a big theme park.

I have some love for B1 and B2, but this one leaves me no memory. It's compelling to play, it works, but it's not a gaming moment I guess.

Still, it's an honest game, that does some things very well and fail on others. Compare to what steam ratings mean for other single player games it should be at least good, bordering on very good IMO.

I'm a long time Borderlands fan, back from the very beginning. This is the first one I didn't buy at launch, partly because of the negative buzz around it, and partly because Randy Pitchford is a vile dork who should not be in charge of anything. 

Eventually, though, I picked it up on sale and... it's rad af. 

You'll see a lot of negative reviews saying things like "Best combat and gunplay in the series, but it's bad because XYZ." 

Well just what in the hell is there to Borderlands apart from those two things? Story? Look, apart from the TellTale games, none of the Borderlands games have had Oscar worthy writing. Some wove better tales than others, but the story is and has always been a backdrop for pretty colors and loud explosions and dopamine pouring right into your eyeballs. Nothing has changed here. 

Borderlands 4 offers top shelf action, amazing gunfights with guns that legitimately make you agonize over replacing them, even at early levels. There are certainly weak spots, of course. I didn't really care for the Digirunner vs other, older vehicles types. I thought that the map was perhaps *too* big with not enough to do on it. 

But this isn't close to a bad game, and I've had an absolute blast with it so far. 

If you're not sure, wait until it goes on sale again and scoop it.

I am absolutely sick to death of BL writing. I hate the terrible jokes, and the way the game insists upon itself constantly: Accept a quest and be prepared to stand on that spot for another 3 minutes, listening to ♥♥♥♥♥ dialogue. But don't walk away! they will make you manually interact with an object right next to them in a few minutes when they finally finish talking about their vegetable patch or Chad's obsession with toenail clippings or whatever. Then they'll send you halfway across the map to interact with something else, but not before another couple minutes of dialogue!

It would be far too simple to make it skippable, or provide a HUD pointer to the mission while they continue speaking. Nope. Stand there, and soak in the legendarily tedious "world building" and wait your bloody turn before you resume play.

It is a constant throughout the entire game. I want to shoot stuff, not stand on the spot watching an NPC animate like something from an early 2000s game, spouting "humour" that somehow makes Marvel look like a comedy masterclass.

The shooting is fun (very much BL3 but with some extra movement), but it feels so utterly sterile in this open world environment. After a couple of hours you'll know which areas of the map will be the Doom-like arenas where things spawn in before you even enter. It is about as rote as can be.

The character classes are again "fine," but the build variety just feels so stilted. There's just no room for creativity here at all.

The open world itself is pure Ubi-Slop. Too big for it's own good, the map crammed full of icons and redundant collectibles like an infected petri dish. All the worst elements, with a vehicle too slow to traverse around it efficiently.

Gearbox's Randy Pitchford is an insufferable tool whose presence around the marketing for his games actively reduces my enjoyment even further. the game is exorbitantly priced, performs poorly, and is jammed full of boring, predictable content.

I wouldn't recommend this to anyone but the most ardent BL fans who are willing to tolerate a lot of unnecessary BS.

tl;dr - The technical side of the game is the best in the series imo, but the story, writing, and characters (particularly the recurring ones) are almost completely uninteresting or irritating, which made the game lackluster and disappointing.

Vehicles & Movement
The summonable vehicle was a great change of pace from having run to a station to get one, the glider was fun, and the overall movement felt good. Massive improvement from previous games.

The Guns
The guns are ok, but the lack of (good) scopes on a lot of sniper rifles was especially unsatisfactory. Having grenades be a rechargeable ability was a solid improvement. Still, lots of garbage guns that suck and only few that are good. If I could change anything about this series it'd be the ability to custom design & order guns directly from manufacturers. One could curry favor with specific manufacturers to unlock better tiers of weapons by doing missions for them, or maybe have blueprints for guns &/or components you can find in world or get as quest rewards. I liked that there was more mixing and matching of manufacturer weapons parts, and I would like to see the players be able to use their creativity and ingenuity to come up with their own weapon component combos. Just tired of the "Billions of guns and only 99.9% of them suck!"

The Design
I think Borderlands has always done well with their level design, the weapon aesthetics, and their enemies have looked cool for the most part. I thought the vaults were far better in this game than the others. Having to find relics to open a portal to the vault, then going through waves of enemies before taking on a unique vault guardian was pretty cool! It looked awesome too.

The Writing
The dialogue is overly cringey, and it was an instant headache seeing characters from previous installments (namely Claptrap and Lilith. Please retire these insufferable characters). A big pet peeve of mine is the "therapy speech." It's unpleasant to hear some random savage, or a main character, vomit up their therapy session on a quest. It seems ridiculous that these barbaric worlds have such a thing, and then everyone just blows each other up all the time anyways. I think it's supposed to come across as comedic and relatable, but it's just lame.

Playing another "resistance", underdog style approach in this hellscape felt lazy and unimaginative. I found myself playing the game mostly muted. Other than Zadra in her quest, I really can't remember anything being interesting from the game or its characters. Her character was exciting, cool, and I enjoyed the voice acting. The other quests, particularly the "hold this object in one hand and walk for 5 minutes to put it into scanner" and "slay 5 of these creatures" felt like time padding, were immemorable. Though, the activities (Ancient Crawlers, Silos, Ripper Driller Sites, etc) were alright, and I had fun fighting the Rift Champions when they popped up.

I really disliked Arjay and was initially relieved when he died so early on. Hearing him through the various audio logs I found during play didn't warm me up to him at all. The Crimson Resistance was also just lame. If I could have worked for The Order and smushed them all and kidnapped 

Vault Hunters
I only played Vex all the way through the main quests and she was fun enough. Her lines were alright and liked the voice acting for her, and the other vault hunters were all decent (both voice acting and dialogue-wise) from what I heard.

On va la faire courte : Borderlands 3 réussit son contrat de départ en proposant un bon défouloir, mais la formule commence franchement à fatiguer et laissera sur leur faim ceux qui espéraient un vrai saut franchi par la licence.

En point positif : le gunplay a un super punch et la prise en main est immédiate. C'est fun, nerveux, et le jeu gagne en sensations brutes lors des gunfights. De plus, les quatre classes de Chasseurs de l'Arche sont vraiment différentes les unes des autres. Chaque perso a ses propres mécaniques et sa façon d'aborder le terrain, ce qui évite de tourner en rond pendant les combats. Par contre, le skill tree est assez terne. Il manque de choix vraiment passionnants ou marquants pour pousser le theorycrafting à fond, et on finit souvent par attribuer ses points par défaut plutôt que par vrai enthousiasme.

Visuellement, le jeu reste figé dans ce qu'il maîtrise depuis des années. La direction artistique en cel-shading garde son identité, mais après trois opus majeurs et une flopée de spin-offs, on s'en lasse franchement. Le moteur n'apporte pas cette étincelle de fraîcheur qu'on attendait, et on évolue en terrain trop connu sans jamais être surpris.

Côté écriture, j'ai toujours autant de mal. Alors oui, il faut reconnaître que c'est un peu moins "pipi-caca" que par le passé et qu'on évite quelques lourdeurs d'adolescent, mais la qualité globale des dialogues et du scénario peine à captiver. Les répliques tombent souvent à côté et les antagonistes manquent d'épaisseur. Résultat : on finit par zapper la narration au maximum pour retourner au seul truc qui compte vraiment, dézinguer des vagues d'ennemis et ramasser du loot.

L'une des plus grandes déceptions vient de la structure de son univers. La promesse de voyager de planète en planète laissait espérer un renouvellement de l'exploration, mais sur le terrain, le monde ouvert est d'une platitude affligeante. Les cartes sont inutilement vastes, cruellement vides d'intérêt, et les trajets deviennent vite une corvée. Le level design manque d'inspiration pour donner envie de fouiller chaque recoin.

Et puis bon, parlons de l'aspect technique deux minutes : les performances sont purement et simplement nulles à chier. C'est scandaleux d'avoir un jeu aussi mal optimisé des années après sa sortie. Entre les chutes d'IPS incompréhensibles dès que trois explosions se courent après, les micro-stutters réguliers et la lourdeur globale du moteur qui fait chauffer la bécane pour rien, on se demande ce que les devs ont foutu. Dans mon cas personnel, heureusement, ça reste parfaitement jouable et ça ne m'a pas empêché de faire mon bonhomme de chemin, mais franchement, ça fait tache pour une production de cette envergure.

Borderlands 4 delivers exactly what I was hoping for: fast-paced gunplay, a ridiculous amount of loot, and the signature humor that makes the series so much fun. The gameplay feels smoother than ever, with improved movement and combat that make every fight exciting.

The new Vault Hunters are a blast to play, each offering unique abilities and plenty of build variety. Experimenting with different skills and finding that perfect legendary weapon never stops being satisfying.

The world is packed with personality, memorable characters, and plenty of side content that makes exploration worthwhile. Whether I was tackling story missions, hunting for rare gear, or jumping into co-op with friends, there was always something fun to do.

Like every Borderlands game, it's at its best when you're chasing better loot and sharing the chaos with friends. If you're a fan of the series, this is an easy recommendation, and if you're new to Borderlands, it's a fantastic place to jump in.

well it's a bad Borderlands game, but it's a decent Firefall (edit, Battleborn actually) sequel. 

fails to maintain any of the design choices that made the series stand out and satisfying, leaning way too hard into sci-fi aesthetic while somehow losing any feeling of alien exploration as the world has grown dim and uninteresting. Mechanics that were slowly doled out to the player are suddenly thrust upon you, like the game is impatient with it's own delivery, 2 hours in and I have all weapon slots unlocked and multiple traversal techniques and none of it feels interesting or earned. UI elements are cluttered and illegible, skill trees look amateurish, enemies are almost never distinguishable from their environment. Without even touching on performance (don't even get me started, it's actually embarrassing how poor this runs, shame on you) my issues with design choices run deep. The choice to replace stat descriptions with symbols, instead of making information more immediate, requires you to convert the meaning in your head when comparing items instead of the game just telling you. It is the type of choice that you can feel a manager making without understanding the player experience and why things are done they way they are, you have to actually consider the experience instead of the aesthetics. 

It's genuinely baffling how we got here from what I consider to be my gold standard FPS series from a satisfaction of design standpoint. I wasn't kidding with the Firefall comparison though. Look up gameplay from that old failed MMO and compare to gameplay from previous Borderlands games and tell me this doesn't have more in common with that game. From UI to world design to armor aesthetics to creatures to environment, it's like the copycat became the copied, it's bizarre and disappointing. All in all there is a long line of poor choices that led to the creation of this game obviously, and I'm unsure if the series is salvageable in it's current hands, but I sincerely hope there is reflection and honesty from the studio if there's a chance of them turning around in the future (hey, a boy can dream right?)

Excessive amount of bugs not worth the time nor money

**Boring game.**

First of all, I didn't experience any lag, endless shader compilation, or FPS drops with my 9070 XT. I played the game in August 2026 without the DLC.

However, I encountered three bugs where dialogues would freeze, forcing me to return to the main menu and load back in. Each time, I lost about 10–20 minutes of progress. One of these bugs even happened late in the game, after the main story.

Now, about the game itself. It's just bland. The story is boring and quite short. The humor would probably only work if I were 15 years younger. The same goes for the side missions.

The enemies you encounter in the first three minutes of the game make up about 30% of all enemy types you'll see, including in the final missions.

The activities are repetitive and don't introduce anything new. There are plenty of them, but they're all essentially the same.

The bosses are boring as well. There are only about 2–3 mechanics used across all of them, and they're extremely easy to understand. Defeating bosses doesn't feel rewarding either—you can easily end up with only blue or purple loot. Sure, you can farm them, but what's the point? The developers should have increased the drop rates for the first (story) kill of each boss.

Even the final chests in the Vault only contained green and blue loot.

As for the guns and builds, there are too many stats and effects to read compared to how often you're replacing your weapons. On top of that, the game doesn't provide enough challenge or motivation to dive deeper into the build system, at least throughout the main story. I played on Hard, and in some quests the enemies were 3–5 levels above me.

Some guns are genuinely unique, and the gunplay can be fun, but for the most part it feels mediocre. The enemy variety is lacking, and their AI is poor as well.

Not recommended, especially considering the company's policies and pricing.

If you don't much care about controversial statements of Randy Pitchford, which caused a public outcry at the release, and the obviously inflated price tag (both for the main game and all DLCs), then in the first hours the impressions about the game itself are only good.

This is definitely one of the most dynamic first-person shooters, where I experienced incredible freedom and convenience in terms of flexible character control. You can accelerate, make jumps, double jumps, dash, slide, cling to ledges, quickly use grappling hook, grab explosive objects and throw them, hit the ground with force, hover, climb walls, instantly summon transport and teleport into it and jump out of it just as instantly. All this creates an amazing entertainment experience and unique situations during battles and shootouts.

The main storyline is straightforward and simple, but some of the side-missions are made more creative and interesting with typical Borderlands humour. Open world is definitely overwhelmed with activities and collectibles, but they're easily skippable If you're bored to find them all.

I've not faced any critical errors during the whole walkthrough, but optimization is still leaves much to be desired. So "compiling shaders" simulator is not a joke, but a constant part of the game... and that's sad.

Whatever it is, upon the whole I mostly enjoyed the game, but wish that the devs would polish the technical part and reduce their appetites concerning DLCs price tags.

A mixed bag of a Borderlands game for sure, but one that I still enjoy. The best gunplay, and vault hunters to date. Far less cringe than BL3, but often far less memorable. I'm glad they tried something new with the open world, but I certainly prefer the old style. It is a well crafted world, but as Borderlands is so often about bosses and raids, it is often underused and fails to live up to the variety of the more curated spaces of old games. The new content has been fun and added much needed endgame activities. Now that its polished (for me at least), I'd say its worth it for any BL fan.

As far as I've played, this is a must play for fans of the Borderlands franchise. It has the best gunplay, movement, visuals, and exploration of the series. Obviously, Borderlands 2 is going to have the nostalgia factor working for it. I was replaying 2 & 3 before playing this one (the original borderlands unfortunately is extremely stuttery no matter what I do so I didn't replay it) and this one is by far the most fun to play. I am not too far into the game and will update my review if anything changes, but I'm loving this one. While I don't agree with the things Randy Pitchford said, I am separating him from this game because he is the CEO of Gearbox, and not the lead developer or director of this game. Rating it negatively because of him is an unfair representation of how awesome this game really is.

Now, I'm assuming this game may have had a plethora of issues on launch but they seem to have been fixed in my experience. I'm playing in 1440p with FSR in quality mode and frame gen turned on and the game is extremely smooth with no ghosting and I haven't experienced a single crash. It looks no different than it does with these settings turned off. I never played Borderlands for the graphics, but this is the best looking one yet. I've always admired the unique art style this series carries, but this one really shows it off well. I was surprised by how much better this one looks than the previous games.

The gameplay is extremely fun. I think this one has the best loot-drop rate of the entire series and the weapon variations is immense. I also like the new additions. Being able to call in your vehicle anytime is pretty sweet. The grappling hook is fun and so far I've used it pretty frequently. The open world is perfect to me. I've seen several people say it's empty, but I get lost finding areas to clear out to obtain loot, I keep finding side missions to complete, random boss encounters to defeat, swarms of enemies to obliterate, and plenty of scenes to explore and take in. There is always something to do and I haven't been bored of the game at all.

I haven't kept up with this one as well since it released, I was pretty skeptical after the 3rd installment. I enjoyed Borderlands 3, but the writing was absolutely horrible. It is much better in this game. It seems to go back to its roots while being mixed with modern times (I know Borderlands wasn't too long ago, I grew up with these games. Times have changed very much since the first one). I'm thinking this game fell victim to modern hate culture, where everyone jumps on board to hate on something just because it's popular. Maybe I'm wrong, but I'm having as much fun with this one as I did the first one and that one is one of the most memorable experiences I've ever had in gaming. Give it a shot without falling into the hate. You'll probably have a lot of fun.

I've played the whole Borderlands franchise, including Wonderlands.

I'm a dozen or so hours into this one, and I expect I'll log in at least a hundred hours more because I'm really enjoying it.

No, this is not Borderlands 2. And no, I didn't care for Borderlands 3 even though I wanted to.

No, the story isn't quite as "deep" or coherent as in Borderlands 2 or the Pre-Sequel or the Telltale story games or whatever. But it's closer, and I'm liking it much better than Borderlands 3.

No, beyond the Deluxe Edition I paid half price for during a Steam sale, I refuse to buy the DLCs at full price. I'll wait for them to come down to a cost that isn't insulting.

BUT...

...this game is NOT as bad as all the negative reviews would make out. 

It plays great. I've gone with the recommended graphics settings, and I'm experiencing absolutely no problems. 

And it's FUN--FUN in the way Borderlands was in the first game through the Pre-Sequel (plus Tiny Tina's Wonderlands). In fact, something about it reminds me of the first game, but with all the bells and whistles that technological advances have made possible since the franchise's debut. 

Cool loot everywhere. Insane bosses in crazy missions. Absurd situations, thanks to that insecure, delusional, sociopathic, stair-hating robot, Claptrap. Also lots of likeable oddball NPCs.

I'm not TRYING to like this installment, as was the case with Borderlands 3. I just do.

Get it on sale, no doubt. And then have FUN the way only Borderlands (minus Borderlands 3) can deliver.

I change my review to actually recommend the game for Linux gamer. 
But I still have to be a bit bitter under some specific mechanic and stuff from the game. 
Started playing Borderlands because it got me so much interested about the game back when borderlands 2 was the latest released. 
Loved spending time farming in Borderlands and enjoyed the GOTY remastered, Borderlands 2 was the best game i ever played, loved every bit about that one beside the meta build and OP10 difficulty, TPS was a bit less good, but the Claptastic voyage did redeemed that one so good. 

Borderlands 3 on the other side, was the one i did spent more time, likely over 2k hours only on epicgames, did literally everything in this one, but some stuff where a bit off or needed in Borderlands 4, like the easy sell junk button, that is absolutely insane good, but that doesn't redeem Borderlands 4 from being a bit less capable over every other in the series, the UVH thing is good, not needing to replay the entire story is good, just to have a bit of a challange, surely better then the Mayhem system in Borderlands 3, the 4th lack surely of build variety, poor rafa got nerfed yet again and the other vault hunter actually work under 1 or 2 specific build, the mayhem 20 in the takedown is a good hard challenge strictly for that mode, but still, even by min maxing the build, only some or specific meta build work, specific weapons and stuff, there is no actually a very true "make your own build and use whatever", same problem happened in borderlands 3 and still borderlands 2 got more variety of build  if you don't push OP level.

I will change the review to recommended as if you love the series, this game can actually fill that emptiness we crave. 
For who want to lean inside the Borderlands series, just be ready that you could not enjoy the game as other, making you experience feeling bad and making you regret even buying the game, but as of today every game is not for everyone, so be aware of bad review if they aren't actual fan of the series.

I know I am super late to the party on this game, however I feel compelled to share my experience. I only bought this game because it was on sale, since around release time of this game, lots of users reporting poor graphics performance. Gave it a chance on my GTX 1080Ti (11GB) card. Not good, I had many crashes, even stupid ones, like on pause, or shopping for guns on the gun machine. I even had the power go out once on me and the saved game was corrupted so I had to start all over from a new game. I was on level 30 so a huge bummer there. My computer barely handles the game on lowest graphic setting, and motion is jumpy. 

I can't believe how bad performance is honestly. Just as a comparison, I played Borderlands 3 on my laptop just yesterday (it only has a 6GB Graphics card), and the gaming, motion is nice and smooth. Maybe it's something about the way developers built ONE GIANT MAP on BL4 that could be part of the issue, but I really think they dropped the ball on this release. They need to consult AI or something and get a patch out to help this issue. haha, I know I am wishful. I have never had this much trouble playing a game when I know my hardware is not basic.

Just when I thought things were about as rough as I could get with gameplay performance, I played today and it somehow got worse. I did notice the snowy mountainous area of the map does not handle as well as the other areas though. This is unplayable now, and I think I'm done fooling with this game. When people buy this game, I think it should come with a warning. Like "Recommended for higher-end gaming machines with 24gb GFX cards or better."

Now for my take on the game designs and characters. I am excellent with reading and recognizing voices so you will notice I have more opinion than most on this. I think Gearbox needs to work on their NPC's and get better voice actors that have more personality. Additionally, this game was only mildly humorous, and to me the humor has faded ever since BL1. Even Clap-Trap had only a few comical lines. At least on BL2 you could tell the effort was there. I don't expect anyone to take this seriously, but I could do better, at funnier voices + comedy. I have enough respect for the Borderlands series that I would be willing to help on BL5 or BL6 to make it more entertaining. I might actually enjoy that, and be able to put my money where my mouth is at the same time. Again, not joking.

With characters, I think they are trying too hard to offer diversity - to the point where there are too many females. They force some of it, but never is there a Giant, or Badass that is a female? If you are aiming to please everyone, you could do better than that! I also think Gearbox, in the past has chosen weak BLACK celebrity voice-actors, like Wanda Sykes and Ice-T. Wanda is just annoying, and Ice has always been a mild personality (not many cared for his music either). He has never really been cool or funny. At his age by BL3 he just sounded like a fat, stretched-lip, cranky baby from SoCal. Next time you should be more selective. For example, if you had just ONE boss with Idris Elba's voice and you will have people excited and buying the game even if they have never heard of Borderlands.

I don't usually write reviews, let alone bad ones, but this one feels warranted. 

for context, I'm not a borderlands fanboy. I enjoyed 1&2 but certainly wouldn't say they are in my top games or shooters. So this review is not coming from a biased butthurt opinion, but simply for what the game actually is. 

Leaving the launch issues this game had and performance issues aside,

good
1. This game runs perfect FOR ME, I have not had a single issue thus far regarding performance. 
2. Graphics are fine, nothing ground breaking, but its clean and has the borderlands feel. 
3....thats it. 

BAD
1. The world is big and open, and boring. There is nothing interesting about it. It feels like the landscape was procedurally generated and they just threw some assets on it. 

2. The gunplay is very basic, and the guns themselves are where it falls very short. They don't feel impactful, they don't feel unique, and you mostly get the same "type" of guns with minor variations. This is a franchise that was known for having thousands of "unique guns". Although I don't think they ever truly achieved anything close to that, this just feels like a step backwards. 

3. The difficulty is one of the major crippling factors for me personally. I am playing on the hardest difficulty available (not UVH mode because you need to beat the game first) and I have to TRY and die. It is extremely easy and boring. They try to spice things up by forcing you to swap weapons around based on shields, or armor or what ever. It doesn't matter. 

As for UVH mode, what a horrible idea, because the game is so easy and lacks any sort of challenge on its base hardest difficulty, UHM mode is like saying "our game doesn't become fun and challenging until AFTER you beat the game", and I'm willing to bet that "challenging" just means bigger bullet sponges. 

4. Story and Dialogue. Wow. What a flop. The story is just not there, and the dialogue is horribly weak. Not only is it weak, but its long and keeps you from doing anything until its done. The humor is forced and lacks any depth, as does the rest of the dialogue. You don't really connect with anything in this game, so these long drawn out dialogues are usually followed by you and your friends running around goofing off until they finish talking. 

In fact, that seems to be the true problem with this game...

Bottom Line
The game fails to challenge you and is very boring, With no real depth or character in its design overall, It fails to draw you in or hold your attention for almost anything. The game does not delivery on almost any criteria. 

I gave this game enough hours for a fair shake. if a game is not fun or interesting after 10+ hours, that's not a slow burn, its a lack of fire. I cannot recommend it.
I would recommend to the Devs to let this franchise die or hand it off to a different studio that might shake some sh*t up.

I nervously purchased this at a steep discount off of GMG after reading lots of negative reviews.

To my surprise, it didn't turn out nearly as bad as I expected. Is it poorly optimized? Yes, but I've had much worse experiences with other titles and no one had any complaints about those. I'm not going to touch on developer-community interactions, but purely on playability and game content.

As far as I'm concerned it's about what I've come to expect from the franchise. It's got low brow humor and the jokes are explained out for you, despite needing absolutely zero explanation. It is so bad that I honestly believe it was written by someone with autism, or FOR someone with autism, or both. I mean no ill will towards those with autism--they have their place in society, but someone keep them away from the script. Is this what gen-z thinks is humor? Does every bite of every meal have to be pre-chewed for them? I mean sure, it's perfect for the quick fix dopamine cycle kids. God help us if they have to think about something for it to be funny. ♥♥♥♥ you if you think you're going to light up any additional neural pathways with a hot zinger of a joke that does anything more than bounce off of their forehead. Remember, there is liability in forcing guffaws upon them as they have not mastered the art of breathing and swallowing spit in rapid succession.

"I NEED TO KISS, BUT I CAN'T CAUSE I'M A ROBOT" --paraphrased from yaptrap; cue sitcomlaugh.wav. What even is this ♥♥♥♥? This dialogue should not even exist. It reminds me of the current SNL in its ongoing desperation to remain relevant. Set scene: a cripple attempts to climb the proverbial or literal corporate ladder, but can't, because his legs don't work. He then points out to the crowd that his legs don't work. "Ha-ha, I can't climb it, because my legs don't work." Aromatically speaking, it smells of a fart from a city block away.

"IT'S A REFERENCE!" scream the reddit moderator sitting behind me. Thank you, /r/iamverysmart.

Is there some meta-humor in this joke that was explained when no explanation was necessary in the first place? I honestly cannot tell. Or is the joke that corporate America thinks this is what we consider amusing? Is it that these jokes are so bad they can lead me down a rabbit hole of existential crisis? I can't say for sure. What I can say is that the humor here is the equivalent of soylent green and you're one step closer to being plugged into the matrix and having your prostate milked for protein for consuming it and enjoying it. Imagine if you distilled Norm Macdonald through a series of infinitely-finer coffee filters until he was molecularly and mechanically separated into a homeopathic friendly vapor that happened to infiltrate your sinuses and you've got the general idea of the potency involved in these jokes. It ain't even Lacroix.

Performance wise: I urge you to recall that the previous titles were wildly cartoony and embrace that because you're going to be running it on minimum and despite the potential for greater things you will in fact be playing a game that looks like it is from 2008. The developer has tried to make it something it is not--which is both hyperreal and cartoony simultaneously. There is mutual culpability here between developer and consumer because the demand from the community dictates we need need to be able to inspect the peach fuzz on a rodent's ballsack from 20 feet away and the shareholders are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid or greedy enough to insist it becomes a defining feature of the game. We then scream in agony when our hardware is incapable of rendering it. Just forget about it looking like or performing like a fine-tuned AAA title unless you're cloud computing this ♥♥♥♥ from a data center. I run this ♥♥♥♥♥ in 4k with low settings and FSR turned on to ultra performance and I'm hitting 90-100 fps consistently with yesteryear's hardware and it looks plenty good. My wife is running it on a i7-7700(NON-K VARIANT) and manages reasonable FPS around 60-70. Does it look great? No, it does not, but it runs and looks decent and we can go on with our lives.

If we demanded more quality content in games and gave less of a ♥♥♥♥ about what it looks like we may in the future see inspiration in games when the developers get a break from corporate overlords cracking whips at their backs to please all mouths at once.

In short: It's not as bad as anyone has made it out to be and too many fedora tipping ass goblins are afoot to get an unbiased perspective on this game.

Additionally: I hate all of you, no one is safe, lock your doors at night.
